Major themes include node, graph, and network embeddings; link prediction and relationship inference; community, role, core–periphery, and motif discovery; and anomaly, fraud, spam, and attack detection. Heterogeneous, multiplex, signed, attributed, and temporal networks receive substantial attention, alongside applications in recommendation, social influence, collaboration, citation, and financial forensics.

Typical methods combine random walks, matrix factorization, spectral and topological measures, stochastic blockmodels, latent-space and generative graph models, sampling, sketching, and distributed or GPU algorithms for scalable counting and querying. Deep learning is prominent, including graph convolutional, attention, recurrent, adversarial, autoencoder, and multimodal architectures. Meta-paths, textual content, knowledge bases, and network motifs are repeatedly used to enrich representations.

Recent work emphasizes dynamic and continuous-time embeddings, temporal motifs and change-point detection, robust prediction under evolving or incomplete data, and representations that preserve multiple structural roles or contexts. Other growing directions include heterogeneous graph alignment, graph neural-network security and poisoning attacks, privacy-aware analysis, explainable anomaly detection, and principled benchmarking and evaluation frameworks.

titles<=300|82ba82e6da71ff95be65820342c9.text:
### Differential Privacy for Queries, Data Publishing, and Structured Information

This community focuses on privacy-preserving data release and analysis, dominated by differential privacy (DP). Major themes include private histograms, range and summation queries, datacubes, contingency tables, high-dimensional workloads, and batch linear queries. Research also addresses spatial, trajectory, mobility, and continuous location data, particularly under temporal correlations.

Typical methods include hierarchical decompositions, wavelets, multidimensional partitioning, low-rank and matrix mechanisms, convex optimization, consistency improvements, mixture models, functional mechanisms, random walks, and Bayesian inference. Local DP is increasingly applied to marginal release, recommendation, smart-device data collection, and location preferences. Several works study privacy-preserving mining, including frequent itemsets, graph patterns, data streams, and data cleaning.

A second theme concerns anonymization and adversarial risk: microdata, sparse and unstructured data, search logs, social links, provenance, record linkage, and background knowledge. Studies examine reconstruction, composition, auxiliary-information, and information-fusion attacks, alongside guarantees such as *l*-diversity and policy-based privacy.

Recent trends emphasize utility-aware and workload-aware mechanisms, high-dimensional accuracy, end-to-end parameter tuning, economic selection of epsilon, semantic and policy guarantees, fairness, and systematic evaluation through DPBench. Applications increasingly combine privacy with recommendations, social-media publishing, discrimination prevention, and spatiotemporal event protection.

titles<=300|e7cd6bbb5e54a2190c8131477ac0.text:
## Social Network Dynamics, Influence, and Scalable Graph Analysis

This community studies how opinions, beliefs, influence, and information evolve on complex and signed social networks. Major themes include consensus, disagreement, polarization, social balance, homophily, bounded confidence, susceptibility, private versus expressed opinions, and the interaction between recommendations and opinion formation. Work also examines dynamic and interdependent networks, stochastic effects, external influence, structural change, and epidemic or information diffusion control.

A second major focus is graph measurement and optimization: centrality axioms and variants, node criticality, accessibility, navigability, backbone discovery, coverage, network delay, influence maximization, edge addition or removal, and epidemic mitigation. Typical methods include Markov chains, random walks with restart, shortest- and randomized-path functionals, PageRank, matrix analysis, spectral-radius approximation, dynamical-systems and fluid models, stochastic and threshold processes, Bayesian agents, and simulation. Algorithms emphasize scalability through sampling, greedy and approximation techniques, vertex-centric decomposition, and billion-scale computation.

Recent directions increasingly combine dynamic topology with learning and control: inferring networks from observations or random-walk similarities, active sensing, social-system identification, knowledge segregation, personalized recommendation effects, and intervention through edge recommendations, filters, tagging, or relationship removal. Signed and multilayer settings, heterogeneous agents, and principled centrality characterization are recurring trends.

titles<=300|c117021e22699fb249d76a11a490.text:
### Community Report: Online Ranking and User-Aware Search

This community focuses on improving search and ranking systems through online interaction data, especially for web images, e-commerce, and aggregated search. Major themes include learning to rank with list-level feedback, relevance-aware presentation, heterogeneous result aggregation, and understanding why users search for images.

Typical methods model user behavior through clicks, click sequences, attention, and satisfaction. Online experimentation and exploration are central: papers investigate gradient-space exploration and double Thompson sampling for scalable ranker evaluation. Reinforcement learning is applied to aggregate results from heterogeneous sources, including hierarchical approaches. Other work uses context-aware module embedding learning and models interaction behavior to support more adaptive ranking and presentation layouts.

A recurring emphasis is that ranking quality extends beyond textual relevance: systems must account for display preferences, layout complexity, user context, and behavioral signals. The apparent trend is toward richer, more contextual evaluation and personalization, combining implicit feedback with explicit modeling of attention and satisfaction. At the same time, scalable exploration and reliable online evaluation remain essential for deploying and comparing ranking strategies.

titles<=300|b4ea9edfd19fa0571226765d3b5d.text:
### Data Integration, Entity Resolution, and Human–Machine Data Curation

This community studies how to integrate, clean, and reconcile heterogeneous, noisy, and conflicting data. A central theme is entity resolution and consolidation: blocking, similarity joins, schema and ontology matching, matching dependencies, graph matching, deduplication, and scalable linkage across web, social, spatial, and linked data. Related work addresses truth discovery, source reliability, multiple truths, knowledge fusion, and conflict resolution.

Typical methods combine probabilistic and Bayesian inference, Markov logic, generative models, transfer and active learning, embeddings, locality-sensitive hashing, distributed processing, GPU indexes, and Datalog- or chase-based reasoning. Data-quality research covers holistic repairs, anomaly detection, dependency discovery, uncertainty estimation, and query answering over imperfect data.

Crowdsourcing is a major complementary approach, including human-assisted entity resolution, truth finding, joins, ranking, labeling, and data cleaning. Work optimizes task assignment, worker selection, redundancy, budgets, latency, confidence, and reproducibility, often combining machine predictions with targeted human verification.

Recent directions emphasize deep-learning-based curation and low-resource entity resolution, interpretable risk and quality assessment, active and transfer learning, scalable multimodal or multimodel integration, and systems that provide intelligent assistance for tables, spreadsheets, web extraction, and knowledge graphs. Spatial crowdsourcing and online, adaptive processing also remain prominent.

titles<=300|d640b2234966bd522030ae2ea813.text:
## Scientometrics, Research Assessment, and Academic Performance

This community centers on measuring and explaining research performance, especially in the Italian university and national research systems. Major themes include bibliometric indicators, institutional and individual productivity, university rankings, national research assessment exercises (VQR), peer review, funding allocation, recruitment, and academic career advancement. Studies critically examine ranking distortions, changing evaluation rules, citation windows, field normalization, author order, fractional counting, uncertainty, and the risks of performance-based funding.

A second strong theme concerns collaboration: international, university–industry, public–private, interdisciplinary, and team-size effects on productivity, impact, diversification, and technology transfer. Gender, age, seniority, academic rank, migration, regional divides, and elite or “star” scientists are analyzed as determinants of collaboration and performance.

Typical methods include bibliometric and citation analysis, coauthorship and citation networks, statistical and stochastic models, DEA and efficiency analysis, regression, cluster analysis, benchmarking, sensitivity analysis, funnel plots, and comparisons with peer-review judgments. Author-name disambiguation is addressed through heuristic, unsupervised, semi-supervised, relative-frequency, network, and deep-neural approaches.

Recent work trends toward open scholarly data and infrastructures, machine learning, recommendation systems, semantic multiplexes, predictive assessment, network-based indicators, and more uncertainty-aware, field- and territory-sensitive evaluation.

titles<=300|f4e9f5a18badbcb4db61cc573a28.text:
**Graph Querying, RDF Management, and Heterogeneous Data Integration**

This community centers on querying and managing RDF, knowledge graphs, property graphs, XML, relational databases, and linked data. A dominant theme is the foundations of SPARQL: semantics, complexity, satisfiability, multiset and optional-pattern behavior, negation, query optimization, provenance, updates, federation, and web-scale link traversal. Regular and context-free path queries, navigational expressiveness, graph pattern matching, and query answering over ontologies and rules form a substantial theoretical core.

Typical methods include relational-algebra and datalog-based formalisms, chase and dependency analysis, graph summarization, partitioning, indexing, cardinality estimation, matrix multiplication, compressed storage, incremental view maintenance, and adaptive or cost-based optimization. Systems research emphasizes distributed execution using Spark, HBase, MapReduce, GPUs, cloud platforms, and streaming engines. Benchmarks and empirical studies evaluate SPARQL workloads, federations, geospatial stores, and graph databases.

A second major strand addresses interoperability: mapping relational, XML, RDF, and property-graph models; translating SPARQL, Gremlin, XPath, and SQL-like languages; and developing graph schemas, shape expressions, validation, and evolution mechanisms. Recent directions include scalable federated and stream processing, semantic big-graph analytics, provenance-aware and uncertain graphs, privacy-preserving graph data, visual/query-by-example interfaces, and machine-learning-assisted entity linking, recommendation, and knowledge-graph search.

titles<=300|01c5c4dfb6dc138375c56ee8b846.text:
## Efficient, Fair, and Preference-Aware Search over Complex Data

This community explores scalable search, ranking, and analytics across relational, graph, XML, social, multimedia, biomedical, and hidden-web data. Major themes include top-*k* and skyline queries, preference-aware and uncertain-data querying, similarity and semantic retrieval, OLAP, and distributed or streaming aggregation.

Typical methods emphasize algorithmic and systems efficiency: compressed bitmap and inverted indexes, SIMD/vectorized integer compression, hashing, wavelets, sketches, learned and universal indexes, caching, and GPU acceleration. Researchers also develop crawling, query-reranking, query-planning, approximate retrieval, and adaptive distributed-processing techniques. Graph and social applications include pattern retrieval, expert and product recommendation, peer-to-peer search, and network analysis.

A prominent recent direction is responsible ranking and recommendation. Papers address fairness of exposure and attention, demographic satisfaction, disparate exposure, diversity, polarization, privacy, and coverage, using audits, fairness-aware learning-to-rank, re-ranking, representation design, and antidote data. Retrieval is also shifting toward embeddings, nearest-neighbor search, word-mover’s distance, and biomedical question answering, while multi-stage systems combine learned components with traditional retrieval.

Overall, the work trends toward high-throughput, heterogeneous, interactive analytics coupled with explicit fairness, diversity, and user-preference objectives.

titles<=300|128829780c036d833d43a5ae1070.text:
## Information Retrieval: Neural Ranking, Context, and Search Applications

This community centers on improving information retrieval through learned relevance estimation, query understanding, and context-aware ranking. Major themes include ad hoc document and passage retrieval, web and enterprise search, e-commerce and sponsored search, biomedical and dataset search, expert and entity retrieval, and conversational question answering.

Typical methods have shifted from term-based and axiomatic models, relevance feedback, query expansion, and clustering toward representation learning and neural matching. Embeddings, semantic hashing, kernel pooling, interaction networks, attention, convolutional and recurrent architectures, and listwise, pairwise, and groupwise learning-to-rank are widely used. BERT-based multi-stage re-ranking, weak and selective supervision, adversarial training, reinforcement learning, knowledge graphs, entity linking, and graph embeddings extend these approaches. Personalization commonly exploits session history, implicit feedback, user context, and product neighborhoods.

Recent work emphasizes contextual and conversational search, including query reformulation, answer passage retrieval, history selection, and knowledge-based dialogue. There is also growing attention to unbiased and counterfactual learning from clicks, online evaluation and multileaving, adversarial robustness, interpretability, efficiency, and reproducibility. Application-oriented research increasingly combines retrieval with tables, multimedia, social streams, mobile assistants, and domain-specific knowledge.

titles<=300|fd410ccae100f919f8d7a8648e0b.text:
## Learning-Centered, Distributed Data Management

This community spans database intelligence, scalable transaction processing, and scientific data infrastructure. A major theme is replacing hand-designed optimization components with learned models: deep learning and generative models estimate cardinalities and selectivities, predict resource consumption, choose join orders, tune partitioning, manage views, and support query re-optimization. Learned and adaptive indexes address multidimensional, spatial, genomic, and approximate-range searches.

A second focus is high-performance transactional systems, including multicore OLTP, MVCC and snapshot isolation, serializability, recovery, logging, scheduling, replication, and high-contention execution. Distributed databases study elasticity, placement, availability, consistency, and cross-datacenter transactions, often using dependency logging, Paxos, asymmetric replication, or specialized concurrency protocols.

Blockchain is treated as a data-management platform, with work on verifiable queries, interoperable and permissioned chains, scalable consensus, auditing, and comparisons with distributed databases. Other systems target streams, HTAP workloads, cloud storage, spatial data, video, and large scientific collections.

Typical methods include prototype systems, workload experiments, benchmarks, analytical and probabilistic models, reinforcement learning, deep neural networks, formal consistency analysis, and empirical infrastructure studies. Emerging directions combine databases with deep learning, energy-aware and predictable operation, autonomic administration, approximate processing, and reproducible/open scientific data stewardship.

titles<=300|f0f646a123a599bd69f5567d34b9.text:
## Dynamic Topics and Social Sensing at Scale

This community centers on mining evolving text and social-media streams to discover topics, events, communities, opinions, and behavioral patterns. A major theme is dynamic topic modeling: latent Dirichlet allocation and its extensions include hierarchical, continuous-time, clustered, author-topic, multi-grain, limited-attention, regression-conditioned, and citation-network models. These methods support topic evolution, literature analysis, terminology learning, and trend discovery.

A second focus is real-time social sensing and event intelligence. Twitter and other online sources are used for event detection, burst and substory discovery, timeline generation, rumor and veracity analysis, sentiment and mood sensing, popularity prediction, and situational awareness for disasters, sports, and civil unrest. Health applications are especially prominent, including influenza, dengue, Ebola, autism, and broader disease surveillance and forecasting.

Typical methods combine Bayesian generative models, graph and network analysis, neural embeddings, matrix factorization, incremental and multi-instance learning, probabilistic logic, and differential-equation models. Spatial databases and trajectory methods address localized events, clustering, routing, and optimal facilities.

Recent directions emphasize scalable and continuous-time inference, multimodal and heterogeneous evidence, interactive visual analytics, adaptive representations, and coupling social signals with epidemiological or forecasting models.

titles<=300|88614b9fb5e75dd0f4ddec02337e.text:
## Graph-Centric, Contextual Recommender Systems

This community centers on personalized recommendation, especially collaborative filtering for sparse, implicit, sequential, social, and cold-start settings. Major themes include top-*N* ranking, session and next-item prediction, news, products, media, academic papers, travel, music, and location-based recommendations. Researchers also study diversity–accuracy trade-offs, long-tail exposure, popularity and temporal drift, reputation, trust, spam, privacy, and evaluation.

Typical methods combine matrix/tensor factorization, Bayesian personalized ranking, neighborhood and similarity models, diffusion and random walks on bipartite or tripartite graphs, link prediction, community detection, and latent-factor or topic models. Hybrid approaches integrate reviews, tags, taxonomies, metadata, linked open data, images, text, social relations, and geographic context. Neural methods include autoencoders, neural collaborative filtering, factorization machines, embeddings, attention, GRU/RNN and recurrent latent-variable models. Bandits and reinforcement learning address exploration, feedback, and interactive recommendation.

Recent work emphasizes deep, multimodal, context-aware and session-aware models; visual and textual cold-start recommendation; heterogeneous and social networks; scalable online and distributed computation; interpretable or diversity-aware ranking; temporal modeling; and more robust evaluation in streaming and real-world systems.

titles<=300|c6b8be8b6b6ef4bd58b771f5a924.text:
## Research Evaluation and Academic Performance

This community centers on measuring and explaining research performance, particularly in the Italian university and higher-education system. Major themes include national research assessment exercises (VQR), university and institutional rankings, performance-based funding, recruitment and career advancement, regional and disciplinary strengths, and north–south inequalities. Substantial attention is given to gender differences, academic nepotism, seniority, star scientists, internationalization, and the effects of collaboration, team size, author order, and publication quantity.

Typical methods are bibliometric indicators based on citations, journal metrics, highly cited papers, h/g indexes, and field-standardized measures; data-envelopment analysis, stochastic and statistical models, multivariate and non-parametric methods; network, cluster, sensitivity, and efficiency analyses; and comparisons with informed peer review. Funnel plots and uncertainty analysis address instability in rankings, citation windows, scaling choices, and assessment rules. Author-name and ethnicity disambiguation support large-scale evaluation.

Recent directions emphasize fairer and more robust assessment: fractional and order-sensitive counting, gender-aware analysis, interdisciplinarity, university–industry collaboration and technology transfer, recommendation systems, deep-neural-network disambiguation, career-path prediction, and territorial indicators. The papers consistently question simplistic rankings and warn against poorly designed evaluation and funding systems.

titles<=300|60da8200d67a1e065ce637df557e.text:
## Community Detection in Complex, Dynamic, and Multilayer Networks

This community focuses on discovering and interpreting mesoscale structure in complex networks. Major themes include disjoint, overlapping, fuzzy, hierarchical, core–periphery, link, bipartite, directed, signed, attributed, multiplex, and temporal communities. Applications span social media, co-authorship, mobile and geosocial networks, recommendation, cybersecurity, epidemiology, knowledge graphs, and scientific mapping.

Typical methods include modularity and surprise optimization; spectral clustering, graph cuts, stochastic block models, likelihood and Bayesian inference; label propagation and local vertex-centered processes; personalized PageRank, heat kernels, diffusion, random walks, Markov models, and flow-based techniques; matrix factorization, manifold and density-based clustering; and densest-subgraph, k-core, motif, triangle, and truss methods. Graph signal processing, embeddings, sampling, and scalable distributed or streaming algorithms support large-network analysis.

A strong emphasis is placed on evaluation: quality functions, conductance, detectability thresholds, phase transitions, null models, ground truth, benchmarking, and model-order selection. Recent trends emphasize dynamic and evolving community tracking, multilayer structure, attributed and heterogeneous graphs, local and seeded detection, real-time and linear-scale computation, community profiling and visualization, and integrating network topology with node content, spatial information, and influence.

titles<=300|fc9e32e40a252eb33de839667b8a.text:
## Scholarly Impact, Communication, and Recommendation

This community studies how scholarly work is produced, disseminated, discovered, and evaluated beyond traditional citation counts. Major themes include altmetrics and societal impact; open-access, preprint, repository, and usage effects on citations; scholarly communication through Twitter, Mendeley, ResearchGate, Wikipedia, and policy documents; and bibliometric coverage of books, publishers, datasets, and repositories. A parallel focus is intelligent scholarly infrastructure: paper, venue, researcher, and reviewer recommendation; conference assignment and peer-review systems; metadata extraction, reference resolution, plagiarism detection, and digital-library integration.

Typical methods combine large-scale bibliometric and usage-data analysis with citation, readership, download, social-media, hyperlink, and policy-document indicators. Studies employ network analysis, co-citation and co-readership mapping, text mining, OCR, topic and trend detection, taxonomies, ontologies, surveys, case studies, comparative evaluations, and recommender or classification algorithms. Statistical normalization and field comparisons address heterogeneity, zero inflation, coverage, and indicator validity.

Recent work increasingly treats impact as multidimensional and contextual, linking attention to later citation, usage, and societal or policy influence. It also emphasizes real-time monitoring, preprints and open repositories, persistent identifiers and data citation, automated scholarly workflows, and large-scale social-media and altmetric infrastructures, while critically examining bias, bots, data quality, and unresolved open-access effects.

titles<=300|65f461fea160a172d8f4924b1f9a.text:
## Social Networks, Diffusion, and Collective Attention

This community studies the structure, dynamics, and societal effects of online and offline social networks. Major themes include information diffusion and cascades; popularity, virality, and trends in Twitter, YouTube, Reddit, Facebook, and other platforms; community structure, weak and strong ties, centrality, homophily, and network evolution; and social influence, opinion, emotion, misinformation, and collective behavior. Applications span crisis response, public health, political communication, recommender systems, marketing, criminal-network analysis, scientific collaboration, and online safety.

Typical methods combine large-scale network analysis with community detection, centrality and entropy measures, temporal and spatiotemporal modeling, visualization, and simulation. Diffusion is modeled using epidemic, cascade, survival, point-process, Hawkes, Poisson, logistic, and opinion-dynamics frameworks. Studies also use machine learning, deep temporal models, latent-variable approaches, causal and observational analyses, sentiment and semantic analysis, and mobile-phone or platform trace data.

Recent work increasingly emphasizes prediction and intervention: forecasting popularity, hashtags, engagement, adoption, disasters, and protests; identifying influential users, links, and communities; steering competing cascades and opinions; and evaluating recommendations under interference. Other growing concerns include fake news, social bots, privacy, information overload, online abuse, social bubbles, and the interaction of social and topical structure.

titles<=300|3a29317cda57b87825a1f19d1c84.text:
## Social Networks, Misinformation, and Adversarial Behavior

This community studies online social networks as spaces for information diffusion, political discourse, collective action, and abuse. Major themes include misinformation, rumors, fake news, clickbait, conspiracy narratives, polarization, and extremist or far-right communities. A closely related focus is platform manipulation: social bots, botnets, sockpuppets, crowdturfing, fake profiles, like farms, spam, phishing, and coordinated campaigns. Papers also examine cyberbullying, hate speech, trolling, racism, sexism, and online radicalization.

Typical methods combine graph mining and network modeling with machine learning and natural-language analysis. Researchers use community detection, matrix factorization, latent-space and diffusion models, temporal analysis, link prediction, clustering, sentiment and topic analysis, and supervised or ensemble classifiers. Detection often integrates content, structural, temporal, behavioral, and social-context features; visualization, honeypots, crowdsourcing, and targeted advertising support measurement and investigation. Sybil defenses, privacy/security analyses, ranking interventions, and debunking systems provide countermeasures.

Recent work emphasizes cross-platform influence, political bot operations, manipulation of elections and public opinion, demographic inequalities, filter bubbles, and the role of homophily and polarization in viral misinformation. There is also growing attention to early rumor detection, explainable or trustworthy judgments, authenticity measurement, coordinated adversarial behavior, and systems such as Hoaxy, BotOrNot, and Wikipedia/Wikidata vandalism detectors.

titles<=300|300fcba28910df430f02ab01a404.text:
### Scientometric Mapping and Fair Research Evaluation

This community centers on measuring, mapping, and interpreting scientific and technological impact. Major themes include alternatives and extensions to the journal impact factor and h-index; percentile-, field-, and source-normalized indicators; fractional citation counting; and evaluation of individuals, groups, institutions, countries, and research programs. Many studies address fairness, uncertainty, statistical significance, interdisciplinarity, collaboration, and unintended effects of rankings and national assessment exercises.

Typical methods combine citation, co-citation, co-authorship, co-word, patent, and journal–journal relation networks with clustering, centrality, similarity, regression, principal-component analysis, bootstrap methods, and network growth models. Visualization is prominent, including overlay maps, science and technology maps, historiography, and interactive tools such as VOSviewer, CitNetExplorer, and RPYS. Text mining, topic modeling, MeSH analysis, citation-context analysis, and full-text similarity support research-front detection and knowledge mapping.

Recent work trends toward contextual and semantometrics-based impact assessment, automated identification of milestones and emerging topics, improved author disambiguation and database matching, and comparisons among Web of Science, Scopus, Microsoft Academic, and other sources. There is also growing attention to open citation data, reproducible indicators, research–technology links, global collaboration, and measures capturing interdisciplinarity, influence, and societal relevance beyond raw citation counts.

titles<=300|57ce7617fb3f8c93b5701860e06d.text:
## Network Analysis, Representation, and Dynamic Graph Mining

This community studies methods for understanding large, complex, social, temporal, signed, and heterogeneous networks. Major themes include community detection and role discovery; link prediction, relationship profiling, and tie-strength estimation; node, graph, and network representation learning; centrality, ranking, similarity, and anomaly detection; and graph sampling, sparsification, and scalable motif, triangle, clique, and graphlet counting.

Typical methods combine random walks and restart processes, spectral and matrix-factorization techniques, stochastic block models, modularity and core/truss decompositions, graphlets and higher-order structures, and probabilistic or generative graph models. Sampling-based estimators, MapReduce, distributed processing, streaming algorithms, and external-memory systems address massive graphs. Applications include recommendation, fraud and spam detection, fact checking, social status and attribute inference, epidemic modeling, navigation, and knowledge graphs.

Recent work increasingly emphasizes dynamic and evolving networks, including continuous-time models, change-point detection, temporal anomalies, coevolving multilayer networks, and dynamic embeddings. Representation learning has progressed from DeepWalk, node2vec, struc2vec, and role-based embeddings toward inductive, attributed, heterogeneous, signed, multiscale, and higher-order models. The papers also show growing attention to explainability, fairness, privacy, uncertainty, robustness, and principled evaluation of link prediction and graph generators.

titles<=300|47c5c2f1c7b86912e9d1dbc47846.text:
## Social Media as a Sensor of People, Places, and Politics

This community studies how user-generated and mobile data reveal human preferences, mobility, urban structure, and collective behavior. Major themes include Twitter-based electoral prediction and polarization; geolocation, home/work inference, and migration; urban activity, boundaries, attractiveness, smells, sounds, and walkability; trajectory and contact-network analysis; and applications to retail placement, event popularity, recommendations, churn, and disaster resilience.

Typical methods combine sparse learning, sentiment and topic modeling, text and image classification, probabilistic inference, tensor factorization, and feature learning. Researchers also use graph mining for communities, links, friendships, place networks, and spatial interactions; spatiotemporal clustering and pattern mining for trajectories; and scaling, compression, and optimization techniques for large datasets. Comparisons with polls, firehose data, mobility models, and economic or planning data address validation.

Recent work emphasizes the 2016 U.S. election, fine-grained political affiliation and gender analysis, multimodal content, deep representations, and real-time or country-level geolocation. It also increasingly examines uncertainty, sampling bias, noise, representativeness, privacy-related limitations, and the reliability of social-media traces for measuring populations and forecasting events.

titles<=300|5a97aca7f0ce05d00c947c8b090f.text:
## Dynamic Graphs: Temporal Analysis and Scalable Queries

This community studies algorithms and models for large, evolving, and temporal networks. A major theme is efficient point-to-point distance, shortest-path, and reachability querying, including hop-doubling labels, independent-set labeling, distance sketches, TopCom, Dagger, Hub Accelerator, and reachability oracles. Several works emphasize scalability, provable guarantees, exact computation, and distributed processing.

A second theme is the representation and analysis of time-dependent interactions. Stream graphs, link streams, time-varying graphs, temporal quantities, and semirings provide formal foundations for temporal paths, reachability, centrality, time series, and window-based analytics. Query optimization and order-enforcement techniques address the cost of processing dynamic-graph workloads.

Applications focus on social and information networks: opinion spreading, dynamic monopolies, media gossip, mailing-list threads, trust-aware recommendation, and “small world” reachability. Scientific networks are examined through selection, emergence, and challenge evolution, while graphlets support temporal structure analysis and network comparison.

Recent trends favor unified temporal-algebraic formulations, dynamic indexing, scalable distributed methods, optimized window analytics, and richer structural tools such as dynamic graphlets and network alignment.

titles<=300|f27d30f653e34767d97bb10986d0.text:
## Scalable Data Management and Analytics

This community focuses on making data-intensive computation scalable, adaptive, and interactive. A central theme is query processing: join ordering and optimization, worst-case-optimal and multiway joins, functional dependencies, conjunctive queries, factorized results, hypertree decompositions, and incremental view maintenance. Parallel and distributed execution is studied extensively through MapReduce, dataflow, shared-nothing systems, GPUs, high-speed networks, and skew-aware algorithms.

Graph processing is another major focus, including graph databases, pattern matching, subgraph search, historical and evolving graphs, graph streams, and distributed graph analytics. Systems such as EmptyHeaded, GraphX, Pregelix, AsterixDB, and Ringo illustrate efforts to combine relational, graph, and array processing.

Typical methods include cost-based and randomized optimization, adaptive indexing, sampling and sketches, compression, materialized views, approximate query answering, static program analysis, and worst-case complexity bounds. The papers also explore consistency, transactions, coordination avoidance, privacy, security, provenance, and dataset versioning.

Recent directions emphasize interactive visual exploration, progressive and bounded-error analytics, continuous stream processing, machine learning inside databases, feature engineering, and unified data/ML lifecycle systems. Increasingly, engines exploit heterogeneous hardware, native compilation, adaptive resource management, and specialized representations for large graphs, arrays, tensors, and evolving data.

titles<=300|3b4103bc76434776ff6e254fcc7d.text:
## Database Uncertainty, Repairs, Provenance, and Explainable Querying

This community studies how databases can answer, explain, and repair queries when information is uncertain, incomplete, inconsistent, probabilistic, distributed, or ontology-mediated. Major themes include probabilistic databases and ranking; consistent query answering under integrity constraints; causality, responsibility, diagnosis, and view updates; provenance, data differencing, and workflow reproducibility; and query answering over graphs, trees, XML, incomplete data, and peer-to-peer systems.

Typical methods combine fine-grained complexity analysis and tractability dichotomies with chase procedures, Datalog and disjunctive rewritings, tree automata, provenance circuits, BDDs, knowledge compilation, model counting, belief propagation, and repair programs. Systems work explores relational engines for probabilistic inference, scalable uncertain-data processing, top-k and similarity search, streaming and external-memory algorithms, and tools for data repair, provenance abstraction, debugging, and scientific hypothesis management.

Recent directions emphasize making these techniques practical at scale: dissociation and propagation for approximate inference, read-once and circuit-based query evaluation, cloud-aware provenance and workflow reenactment, graph partitioning, dynamic uncertain-data indexes, and statistical or causal inference over relational data. Other emerging concerns include trust, privacy, crowdsourced uncertainty, data completeness, multidimensional quality assessment, and integration of ontologies with probabilistic and inconsistent information.

titles<=300|12a4d013014e9c8a88124e6ae73b.text:
## Dynamic Social Networks, Influence, and Controversy

This community studies how network structure and evolving interactions shape opinions, influence, information diffusion, polarization, and collective behavior. Major themes include signed networks and structural balance; consensus, disagreement, and bounded-confidence dynamics; social power and dominance; controversy and ideological segregation; epidemic and influence control; and centrality, accessibility, communicability, and node criticality.

Typical methods combine mathematical dynamical models—DeGroot–Friedkin, Markovian agents, threshold, susceptibility, random-walk, and state-flipping models—with spectral analysis, matrix formulations, optimization, approximation algorithms, sampling, and genetic algorithms. Researchers design or evaluate interventions such as edge recommendation, link modification, censorship shocks, contrarian-content exposure, filtering, node removal, and investment across competing camps. Scalable graph algorithms address PageRank, betweenness, link prediction, node discovery, backbone extraction, random-walk domination, and network delay.

A strong empirical strand analyzes Twitter and other online platforms through topic, sentiment, ideological-leaning, attention, and temporal interaction data, including climate, refugee, Egyptian political, and Chinese Wikipedia cases. Recent directions emphasize dynamic topologies, heterogeneous thresholds and activation, multiplex or topic-specific behavior, information diets, and scalable methods for massive graphs. Web crawling and social-system identification provide supporting infrastructure for measuring evolving network activity.

titles<=300|92e3d49eeba5fb63ba4aa7955442.text:
### Complex Data Warehousing, Optimization, and Benchmarking

This community focuses on engineering and evaluating data warehouses for complex, heterogeneous, and web-derived data. XML warehousing and OLAP are central themes, including XML tree patterns, complex hierarchies, summarizability, roll-up operators, query processing, fragmentation, and join indexes. Related work addresses object-oriented and document-oriented databases, biomedical and archaeological data, and personalized medicine.

A major research line concerns warehouse performance optimization through automated selection of indexes, bitmap join indexes, materialized views, and their joint configurations. Typical methods include query and workload clustering, affinity-based and k-means fragmentation, frequent-itemset mining, attribute-dependency analysis, cost models, and Markov analysis for view replacement. Simulation and generic benchmarking tools are widely used to evaluate clustering, CRUD operations, indexing, and database-system performance.

The community also develops benchmarks such as XWeb, DWeb, OCB, and LSHTC, covering warehouses, object-oriented systems, and large-scale text classification. More recent directions extend optimization to public clouds and shared optimizations, explore document-based architectures and asynchronous replication, and apply warehousing and OLAP to web data, Twitter trends, and complex domain data.

titles<=300|363af111f6bcff27aeea289e14d6.text:
## Network Science for Scholarly Information and Society

This community studies networks as models for scientific communication, information retrieval, and social influence. Major themes include bibliometrics and research evaluation: PageRank, citation-based prestige, author impact, h-index alternatives, journal metrics, rising-star detection, research trajectories, and credit allocation. Coauthorship and citation networks are used to analyze collaboration, communities, power, vulnerability, and gender asymmetries.

A second major theme is bibliometric-enhanced information retrieval. Work addresses query and term expansion, thesaurus and terminology mapping, expert search, learning to rank, personalized retrieval, visual search interfaces, knowledge maps, semantic heterogeneity, and interactive browsing. Author-name disambiguation, entity matching, author identifiers, and metadata enrichment are recurring practical problems.

Typical methods include graph centrality and PageRank variants, Google-matrix and spectral analysis, community detection, clustering, link prediction, Markov-chain models, regression, graphons, mean-field approaches, and scalable MapReduce algorithms. Researchers combine citation, coauthorship, bibliographic, and usage-log data with visual analytics and human evaluation.

Recent directions broaden network analysis beyond scholarly graphs to Wikipedia, social media, patents, corporate control, Bitcoin, food cultures, and street networks. They emphasize dynamic and multiplex networks, uncertainty and data quality, cross-cultural comparisons, emerging-technology prediction, semantic and visual interfaces, and integrated science models for discovery and recommendation.

titles<=300|f26565b1f457c1d37a3691bfb0c3.text:
## Efficient Search, Analytics, and Preference-Aware Data Systems

This community focuses on scalable data management and information retrieval. Major themes include top-*k*, skyline, ranking, and preference queries; hidden- and web-database crawling; OLAP and multidimensional analytics; bitmap and inverted-index compression; similarity and nearest-neighbor retrieval; and search over social, XML, graph, and scientific-workflow data.

Typical methods are algorithmic and systems-oriented: SIMD and GPU acceleration, compressed bitmaps, vectorized integer decoding, hashing, wavelet histograms, column and row reordering, caching, and distributed or in-memory dataflow. Query processing emphasizes adaptive aggregation, approximate estimation, sliding-window monitoring, skyline joins, rank-aware inference, and efficient subset or similarity search. Machine-learning methods include embeddings, word mover’s distance, clustering, and probabilistic or relational models.

Recent directions emphasize high-throughput analytics over massive or dynamic data, including trillion-cell interaction, graph and relationship analytics, distributed streams, and scalable key-value indexing. Retrieval is increasingly semantic and neural-inspired rather than purely term-based, while systems also address result diversification, fairness in ranking, privacy, and user preference elicitation. Social and hidden-web applications remain prominent, combining crawling, recommendation, marketplace interaction, and personalized search.

titles<=300|8f4d7d025c2f9283195624062566.text:
## Graph Querying, Semantics, and Scalable RDF Management

This community studies querying and managing RDF, semantic-web, XML, and property-graph data. Major themes include SPARQL semantics and complexity—especially joins, optional patterns, negation, satisfiability, well-designed queries, paths, and updates—alongside ontology-mediated answering, existential rules, schema reasoning, and incomplete or annotated information. A substantial body of work addresses graph navigation, regular and context-free path queries, traversal languages, relational foundations, and reconciliation between RDF and property graphs.

Typical methods combine formal expressiveness and complexity analysis with query rewriting, schema- and partition-based indexing, summaries, compression, cost and join-size estimation, and incremental view maintenance. Systems research emphasizes distributed and federated execution, replication, MapReduce/Spark/GPU processing, adaptive partitioning, stream reasoning, and secondary-memory storage. Benchmarks, workload analysis, and practical studies evaluate real query logs and large RDF deployments.

Other recurring concerns are XML–RDF interoperability, schema and shape languages, provenance, data completeness, visualization, entity suggestion/linking, and geospatial or cube analytics. Recent directions emphasize heterogeneous graph querying, web-scale federation, streaming and historical graphs, interactive visual builders, uncertainty and privacy-preserving graph representations, and unified foundations for emerging graph query languages.

titles<=300|190ac2cf66ecb94a05ba0bebc6ec.text:
## Scalable, Scientific, and Energy-Aware Data Management

This community studies how database systems can scale across multicore hardware, clusters, clouds, and geographically distributed environments while preserving performance, consistency, and availability. Major themes include parallel OLTP, transaction processing and recovery, MVCC and serializability, distributed transactions, replication, partitioning, and data placement. Work also addresses main-memory and hybrid OLTP/OLAP systems, log-structured storage, autonomic resource management, and the tradeoffs between latency, consistency, energy use, and hardware efficiency.

Scientific and spatial data management is another central focus. Papers describe relational backends for finite-element and astronomical data, array systems, multidimensional and spherical indexes, spatial joins and cross-matching, scientific metadata, online observatories, and large geo-tagged datasets. Several works connect database infrastructure with astronomy and broader scientific data practices.

Typical methods include concurrency-control and snapshot-isolation designs, dependency and logical logging, Paxos-based replication, graph-based partitioning, adaptive resource and replica selection, predictive modeling, learned indexes, hierarchical triangular meshes, probabilistic joins, and SQL-based interfaces. Recent trends emphasize cloud elasticity, multi-datacenter consistency, scalable distributed transactions, autonomic and energy-efficient systems, predictive buffer and workload management, and integrating databases more directly into reproducible, online scientific workflows.

titles<=300|206cd9a7a1f8494c2b75cdcbf0c2.text:
## Social Diffusion, Influence, and Popularity in Networked Platforms

This community studies how information, opinions, products, epidemics, and malicious content spread through social and temporal networks. Major themes include influence maximization and viral marketing; diffusion-source localization and cascade reconstruction from partial observations; epidemic containment, vaccination, rumor blocking, and cyberbullying control; opinion dynamics and social learning; and prediction of popularity, engagement, adoption, and virality across Twitter, YouTube, Reddit, crowdfunding, and other platforms.

Typical methods combine graph theory, network centrality, epidemic and contagion models, point processes (especially Hawkes and Poisson processes), survival analysis, Bayesian inference, sparse recovery, and stochastic differential equations. Optimization is prominent, including submodular and adaptive influence maximization, optimal control, sequential seeding, incentive allocation, robust optimization, and resource-constrained sampling. Empirical studies use cascades, temporal activity, multimodal content, field experiments, and causal analysis.

Recent work increasingly addresses dynamic, adaptive, multilayer, and non-stationary networks; partial observation, hidden nodes, uncertain transmission, and privacy; competitive or coexisting cascades; higher-order and opinion-aware influence; and real-time or online decision-making. Deep temporal models, attention mechanisms, contrastive learning, and multimodal features are emerging for popularity and cascade forecasting, alongside scalable and robust algorithms for large social streams.

titles<=300|db4b21d53764df5e074f253148ba.text:
## Complex Networks for Science, Software, and Collaboration

This community studies how network structure reveals organization, evolution, and interdisciplinarity across scientific, software, web, social, and healthcare systems. Major themes include community structure in complex software networks; link and group structure in websites and information networks; scientific collaboration and citation dynamics; and the consistency and comparative quality of online bibliographic databases.

Typical methods include complex-network modeling and review, empirical comparisons of network-sampling techniques, network simplification, community-detection algorithms, node-mixing analysis, and centrality measures—especially betweenness centrality as a mechanism shaping collaboration-network growth. Evolutionary models address preferential attachment, citation dynamics, and multilevel, cross-time changes in scientific collaboration. Studies also use web search engines and network-based statistical comparisons to quantify interdisciplinarity, database consistency, and citation topology.

Recent work increasingly connects structural network measures with researcher and field trajectories, examining the impact and life course of interdisciplinarity in computer science. The scope also broadens from analyzing isolated networks toward comparing representations across databases, evaluating sampling and simplification effectiveness, and applying social-network frameworks to real-world healthcare collaboration.

titles<=300|fdc3c3d00c56dedf8912454d5c80.text:
## Community Detection in Static, Dynamic, and Multilayer Networks

This community centers on detecting, evaluating, and interpreting mesoscale structure in complex networks. Major themes include disjoint, overlapping, fuzzy, bipartite, signed, attributed, directed, multiplex, and core–periphery communities, as well as local, small, and hierarchical structures. Dynamic-network research addresses temporal community discovery, tracking, evolution, persistence, streaming interaction data, and real-time event detection.

Typical methods include modularity optimization and multiscale Markov-time approaches; spectral clustering, graph Laplacians, eigenvectors, non-backtracking matrices, and personalized PageRank; label propagation and seed expansion; random walks, diffusion, heat kernels, conductance, and flow-based methods; matrix factorization, manifold and density-based clustering; and stochastic block models, mixed-membership models, and degree-corrected variants. Distributed, parallel, linear-time, sublinear, and memory-limited algorithms target very large graphs.

A substantial methodological strand develops quality functions, null models, detectability theory, phase transitions, model selection, and benchmarks using ground truth, attributes, hashtags, and social-media data. Recent trends emphasize multilayer and temporal modeling, attributed and partially observed networks, semi-supervised and locally adaptive detection, scalable streaming and distributed computation, and integration with graph signal processing, influence maximization, anomaly detection, visualization, epidemiology, and information diffusion.

titles<=300|4d7580ff9242f56d3928f4bc3ede.text:
## Dynamic Topic Modeling and Social-Stream Intelligence

This community centers on discovering, tracking, and explaining topics, events, and communities in evolving text collections. A major theme is dynamic topic modeling: LDA, hierarchical Dirichlet processes, clustered and continuous-time models, author-topic models, topic regression, limited-attention models, and multi-grain approaches recover topic birth, evolution, structure, and influence. Applications span scientific literature, Wikipedia, online reviews, hypertext, and social media.

A second focus is real-time event detection and summarization from Twitter and other streams, including sports, disasters, breaking news, clandestine activity, and localized events. Disease surveillance is especially prominent, using social signals and Wikipedia to detect or forecast influenza, dengue, Ebola, and other outbreaks. Related work studies sentiment, moods, opinions, user preferences, revisit behavior, and social influence.

Typical methods combine Bayesian generative modeling, incremental machine learning, neural embeddings, matrix factorization, probabilistic reasoning, interaction and citation graphs, semantic filtering, ontologies, WordNet, and fuzzy logic. Query expansion, question answering, visualization, and provenance support retrieval and interpretation.

Recent trends emphasize scalable and continuous-time inference, heterogeneous and geo-temporal evidence, cross-lingual timelines, online visual analytics, neural representations, and integrated graph-content models for timely situational awareness and hypothesis generation.

titles<=300|c74b2f0ed36f49504895e6502e09.text:
### Scientometric Mapping, Metrics, and Research Evaluation

This community centers on measuring, mapping, and explaining scientific and technological activity. Major themes include citation impact, journal and author prestige, research excellence, interdisciplinarity, collaboration, knowledge diffusion, innovation, and the historical emergence of research fronts. A substantial strand critiques and improves the journal impact factor, h-index, percentile indicators, Crown indicators, SNIP, SJR, I3, PageRank-based measures, and newer multidimensional or fairness-oriented metrics.

Typical methods combine co-citation, bibliographic coupling, co-authorship, co-occurrence, and citation-network analysis with clustering, community detection, overlay maps, historiography, RPYS, topic modeling, and visualization. Researchers compare Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, Microsoft Academic, patents, and institutional datasets; apply field normalization, fractional counting, percentile ranks, statistical testing, regression, and network models. Author disambiguation and large-scale graph construction are recurring technical challenges.

Recent work moves toward contextual and full-text citation analysis, semantometrics, citation recommendation and summarization, deep-learning prediction, automated surveys, and detection of emerging technologies or breakthrough papers. It also emphasizes open-access measurement, reproducibility, uncertainty, peer-review validation, responsible evaluation, and the social consequences of rankings and performance-based funding.

titles<=300|ca665a09ec99d8cd2172112f4dcd.text:
## Online Social Networks and Complex Network Dynamics

This community studies the structure, evolution, and societal consequences of online and communication networks. Major themes include community detection, centrality, influence maximization, information diffusion, contagion, weak and strong ties, resilience, and link formation or decay. Researchers also examine social-media behavior, popularity, lurking, engagement, friendship, collaboration, and cross-platform interaction.

Typical methods combine large-scale graph analysis with statistical modeling, machine learning, and simulation. Common approaches include Louvain and adaptive clustering, entropy- and fractal-dimension-based network measures, random and geometric graph models, latent-space and discrete-choice models, Hawkes processes, agent-based simulations, epidemic and delay-differential models, and fluid limits of threshold cascades. Supervised and semi-supervised classifiers infer demographics, churn, criminal groups, mental-health risk, and anomalous or suspicious behavior from network and usage data. Mobile-phone, Facebook, Twitter, gaming, Pinterest, GitHub, and web-extraction datasets are prominent.

Recent directions emphasize dynamic, multilayer, spatial, and adaptive networks; temporal analysis of influence, interaction decay, and user behavior; and more realistic models combining homophily, geography, media, preferences, and network structure. Applications increasingly target privacy and contextual integrity, misinformation and targeted diffusion, criminal-network investigation, infectious-disease modeling, recommendation, resilience, and behavioral or demographic prediction.

titles<=300|d34115954e22f8dd7b3298c80c9e.text:
## Text Mining, Mathematical Information Retrieval, and Semantic Search

This community centers on **text classification and clustering**, with applications in authorship attribution, multilingual and short-text categorization, sentiment and opinion analysis, document-type recognition, and hierarchical classification. Common methods include multinomial mixtures, naïve Bayes, k-nearest neighbors, k-medoids, association rules, term-class relevance measures, semantic relations, topic models, feature selection, evolutionary optimization, and similarity-based classification. Active learning and reliability estimation support technology-assisted review and robust categorization.

A second major theme is **efficient similarity search**. Hashing methods—including self-taught, deep discrete supervised, density-sensitive, and topic/tag-enhanced hashing—target short texts, images, and massive-scale time series. Graph analysis and symbolic representations further support classification and retrieval.

Many papers address **mathematical information retrieval and digital libraries**, including formula repositories, LaTeX acquisition, identifier namespaces, formula indexing, Math-aware retrieval, combined text–formula queries, search-engine scalability, mathematical rendering, and searchable Wikipedia. Evaluation compares presentation- and content-based search and query-result merging.

Additional work explores semantic visualization, corpus navigation, web-page segmentation and quality evaluation, personalized keyword extraction, hashtag recommendation, and content customization. Overall, the research trends toward deep and semantic representations, scalable hashing and crawling, interactive/personalized retrieval, and integrated mathematical knowledge management.

titles<=300|5b12100a9816e29f2eccc49b6e5c.text:
### Scholarly Impact, Open Science, and Research Analytics

This community studies how scholarly impact, communication, and discovery are changing beyond traditional journal citations. A dominant theme is **altmetrics**: validating relationships among citations, downloads, Mendeley readership, tweets, blogs, Wikipedia, policy documents, and F1000Prime assessments; assessing data coverage, heterogeneity, bias, bots, zero inflation, and disciplinary differences; and testing whether these measures capture societal impact or research quality. Related work develops article-, author-, journal-, publisher-, institutional-, and book-level indicators.

A second major theme is **open access and scholarly infrastructure**, including green and gold OA, repositories, arXiv, preprints, data linking, metadata, usage histories, and their effects on citations, downloads, and social attention. Studies often find effects vary by field, article age, journal, and selection bias.

The community also develops **recommender and decision-support systems** for papers, venues, experts, reviewers, and conference assignments, using citation, content, taxonomy, usage, social-network, and direction-aware analyses. Peer-review management, scholarly social networks, and academic information behavior are recurring applications.

Typical methods include large-scale bibliometric and webometric analyses, network modeling, social-media mining, surveys, machine learning, scraping and API collection, visualization, normalization, and empirical comparison of indicators.

Recent trends emphasize real-time tracking, policy and societal impact, multidimensional evaluation, institutional assessment, preprint ecosystems, research data, and more robust contextualized metrics.

titles<=300|897b4094fd05a6152cc8b1df76b4.text:
## Multilayer Social Networks, Diffusion, and Social Intelligence

This community centers on modeling and analyzing social systems as multilayer, multiplex, multidimensional, and heterogeneous networks. Major themes include community and group evolution, social roles, influential users, centrality, shortest paths, network robustness, and the discovery of essential relationships. A second strong focus is information diffusion: viral campaigns, innovation, opinion propagation, competing cascades, epidemic containment, immunization, and seed selection across interconnected layers.

Typical methods combine graph algorithms and statistical modeling, including Louvain and Infomap clustering, PageRank and alternative centrality measures, convex optimization, tensor decomposition, branching processes, agent-based models, probabilistic data fusion, and network-based classification. Researchers also use temporal graphs, sliding windows, association rules, language models, sentiment analysis, and structural or textual similarity.

Applications span social media, blogs, reviews, telecommunications, virtual worlds, human resources, health campaigns, and online-offline social integration. Identity resolution and network alignment are recurring practical problems, including profile matching, record linkage, genealogical reconstruction, and cross-device association. Information retrieval work addresses pseudo-query reformulation, document normalization, ranking, and synthetic relevance signals.

Recent directions emphasize dynamic and multilayer settings, heterogeneous statistics, large-scale parallel processing, improved diffusion-aware sampling, missing-data and attack robustness, visual analytics, and the fusion of content, behavior, and network structure.

titles<=300|f93229f9833c19d6a9c709488cad.text:
### Epidemic Modeling on Complex Networks

This community studies epidemic propagation and control-related quantities on complex networks, with emphasis on SIS and SIRS dynamics. Core themes include epidemic cost, propagation behavior, epidemic thresholds, and the relationship between exact and approximate models.

Typical methods combine random-matrix analysis, deterministic network epidemic dynamics, exact Markov-chain formulations, and approximated epidemic models. Several works focus on deriving or improving bounds for the epidemic threshold of exact SIS models, while others analyze how closely approximations represent exact network processes. The inclusion of SIRS models extends the scope beyond SIS dynamics and highlights comparisons between exact Markov-chain descriptions and approximations.

Recent trends point toward greater precision and systematic validation: moving from general analyses of epidemic dynamics and cost to tighter threshold bounds and explicit assessments of concurrence between exact and approximate models. Overall, the papers reflect an effort to balance mathematically tractable approximations with faithful descriptions of epidemic behavior on complex networks.

titles<=300|da79dec823796230d86363053212.text:
## Computational Social Media: Misinformation, Politics, and Online Behavior

This community studies how information, influence, and harmful behavior emerge and spread across Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, Wikipedia, forums, and other platforms. Major themes include political communication and elections; misinformation, rumors, fake news, and conspiracy narratives; social bots, trolls, astroturfing, spam, and Sybil attacks; polarization, echo chambers, censorship, and bias; and online abuse, cyberbullying, extremism, and gender or racial inequality. Additional work applies social media to crises, public health, mobility, employment, food practices, and civic engagement.

Typical methods combine natural-language processing, sentiment and emotion analysis, stance and topic classification, and abuse or clickbait detection with graph analysis of followers, retweets, replies, diffusion, and communities. Researchers use supervised, semi-supervised, ensemble, neural, sparse, and weak-learning models, alongside temporal analysis, agent-based modeling, crowdsourcing, multimodal image-text analysis, and large-scale datasets or monitoring systems.

Recent work emphasizes early detection and intervention: credible rumor debunking, misinformation targeting, real-time crisis and bot monitoring, and platform defenses against manipulation. Studies increasingly incorporate social context, propagation dynamics, multimodal evidence, cross-platform effects, and fine-grained analyses of political campaigns and coordinated influence operations.

titles<=300|ad6792703f1fb90bc5e8a09f0cfc.text:
## Geosocial Intelligence and Urban Dynamics

This community studies how social-media, mobility, and location-based data reveal human behavior, social structure, and urban change. Major themes include geolocation and user profiling; human mobility, commuting, migration, and spatial interaction; urban activity, attractiveness, deprivation, public-space use, and neighborhood boundaries; and applications such as business-site selection, route and food recommendations, event participation, public health, and disaster resilience.

A second strong theme is social-network analysis: community detection, political and extremist-network structure, friendship and influence, antagonistic or allied groups, link prediction, user-list curation, and multiview network fusion. Researchers also infer latent demographics, gender, age, traits, sentiment, credibility, and behavioral patterns from text, follows, images, and interaction networks.

Typical methods include nonnegative matrix and tensor factorization, probabilistic inference, grid-based classification, machine learning and deep feature learning, graph optimization, density-based clustering, total-variation minimization, trajectory compression and mining, spatial databases, and scalable stream processing. Visualization and geospatial analytics are central.

Recent work emphasizes large-scale, multimodal and multilayer data; real-time detection of bursts, crowds, and events; uncertainty-aware geolocation and trajectories; privacy preservation; representativeness and dataset bias; and integrating social traces with mobility or urban-planning models.

titles<=300|5540a75e9836898b80d0b8ab6791.text:
## Recommendation Systems: From Collaborative Filtering to Contextual, Multimodal Intelligence

This community focuses on personalized recommendation across products, news, movies, music, fashion, artwork, apps, points of interest, advertising, and social or reciprocal platforms. Core themes include collaborative filtering and top-*n* ranking; sequential, session-based, and repeat-aware recommendation; cold-start and long-tail settings; social, trust, and knowledge-aware personalization; and complementary or substitutable product discovery.

Typical methods range from matrix factorization, Bayesian personalized ranking, factorization machines, neighborhood models, graph and bipartite ranking, and topic models to neural collaborative filtering, autoencoders, variational models, recurrent and convolutional networks, attention, transformers/self-attention, and embedding methods. Side information includes text, reviews, tags, images, video, audio, taxonomies, linked data, knowledge graphs, location, time, and user behavior. Several works address scalability, approximate similarity search, real-time serving, interpretability, fairness, causal inference, and exploration through bandits or reinforcement learning.

Recent trends emphasize multimodal and cross-domain representations, context- and geo-temporal sequence modeling, graph neural and hyperbolic models, adversarial robustness, causal and fair recommendation, explainability, and meta-learning for algorithm selection. Synthetic sequence generation, public evaluation environments, and large-scale industrial systems also support experimentation and deployment.

titles<=300|8b39a14c8495cffaa4c3336f426f.text:
## Neural, Semantic, and Scalable Information Retrieval

This community focuses on improving search quality, interpretation, and efficiency across web, biomedical, social-media, e-commerce, table, entity, and conversational retrieval. Major themes include neural relevance ranking and semantic matching; query expansion, reformulation, segmentation, and session search; entity linking, disambiguation, consolidation, and relationship retrieval; web-content quality, spam, credibility, and adversarial robustness; and question answering over documents, tables, knowledge graphs, and community content.

Typical methods combine learning-to-rank, pairwise/listwise optimization, online learning, bandits, multileaving, and click or weak supervision. Deep architectures include CNNs, RNNs/LSTMs, attention, sequence-to-sequence models, kernel pooling, MatchPyramid, PACRR, DRMM, interaction models, and generative–discriminative approaches. Word/entity embeddings, language models, graph and discourse features, relevance feedback, and fusion integrate lexical and semantic evidence. Approximate nearest-neighbor search, locality-sensitive hashing, similarity joins, GPU indexing, and distributed evaluation address scale.

Recent work trends toward end-to-end neural and hybrid multi-stage ranking, personalized and context-aware search, explainability, privacy-preserving model sharing, unbiased online evaluation, and retrieval for conversational assistants. Applications increasingly use structured resources—Wikipedia, knowledge graphs, scientific formulas, tables, and electronic health records—while emphasizing factuality, objectivity, recall, and real-world robustness.

titles<=300|f1a3e69700a483cb060806818f24.text:
## Scalable Analysis and Modeling of Complex Social Networks

This community focuses on extracting structure, dynamics, and behavior from large social, information, biological, and communication networks. Major themes include community and role discovery (including overlapping, hierarchical, directed, spatial, and dynamic communities), dense-subgraph, core, truss, and nucleus decompositions, and centrality, ranking, similarity, and influence analysis. A substantial body of work addresses graph sampling and reconstruction, including random walks, wedge and edge sampling, respondent-driven sampling, streaming samples, and methods with accuracy or privacy guarantees.

Typical methods combine spectral and tensor techniques, matrix completion, Markov chains, graphlets and motifs, modularity and null models, probabilistic latent-variable and attribute-based models, and distributed MapReduce or parallel algorithms. Graph generators and sparsification methods target realistic clustering, degree distributions, community structure, and scale-free behavior.

Applications include link prediction and recommendation, viral marketing, fraud and spam detection, insider-trading and anomaly detection, privacy and attribute inference, social influence, political violence, infection spread, and software or citation networks.

Recent directions emphasize dynamic and streaming graphs, change-point and temporal-community detection, scalable triangle and graphlet counting, higher-order network structure, topology-preserving sampling and sparsification, spatial and attributed networks, and practical toolkits and repositories for large-scale analysis.

titles<=300|35110fa9c26312da346b2cd0a4dd.text:
## Network Representation, Link Prediction, and Evolving Graphs

This community centers on learning from complex networks, especially **node and graph representation**, **link prediction**, and **community detection**. A major focus is heterogeneous information networks, knowledge graphs, social networks, citation networks, and recommender systems. Other recurring themes include signed and directed networks, multilayer/multiplex structure, network alignment, similarity search, anomaly detection, and structural roles.

Typical methods include random walks and restart processes (DeepWalk, node2vec, SimRank), matrix factorization, spectral and eigenvector techniques, graph clustering, stochastic block models, probabilistic latent-space models, and supervised or semi-supervised learning. More recent work uses graph neural and deep embedding architectures, attention, autoencoders, nonlinear modularity, and content- or metadata-enhanced representations. Bayesian inference, Markov chains, tensor methods, and optimization are also common.

Recent trends emphasize **dynamic and temporal graphs**, including continuous-time prediction, evolving embeddings, change-point detection, temporal motifs, event graphs, and higher-order dependencies. Research increasingly addresses scalability through approximate search, sparse or low-rank methods, streaming algorithms, and succinct indexes. There is also growing interest in inductive learning, explainable recommendation, robustness, negative links, structural identity, and combining topology with text, semantics, and auxiliary information.

titles<=300|a5d52c533d5f16f59c270d7ea46a.text:
## Graph-Based, Personalized Recommendation and Information Filtering

This community centers on recommender systems, especially collaborative filtering, ranking, and information filtering. Major themes include graph- and network-based recommendation, social and trust-aware personalization, tag and content-enhanced systems, group and context-aware recommendation, and scholarly or digital-library discovery. Cold-start prediction, diversity–accuracy trade-offs, temporal drift, popularity, feedback loops, and evaluation bias are recurring concerns.

Typical methods include matrix and tensor factorization, neighborhood models, latent preference and probabilistic models, diffusion and heat-conduction processes on bipartite or heterogeneous graphs, PageRank-like ranking, clustering, link prediction, and reputation or authority scoring. Hybrid systems combine ratings with text, tags, locations, social ties, trust, or ontologies. Neural networks, autoencoders, recurrent models, and deep reinforcement learning address session recommendation, negative feedback, exploration–exploitation, and sponsored ranking. Active learning, granular association rules, and preference elicitation target sparse or cold-start settings.

Related work covers keyphrase extraction, summarization, citation matching, entity resolution, and semantic publishing as inputs to retrieval and scholarly recommendation. Emerging directions emphasize privacy-preserving personalization, robust and unbiased ranking under spam and position-biased feedback, temporal and behavioral modeling, large-scale distributed infrastructure, and real-world deployment in academia, news, mobile, cable television, and commerce.

titles<=300|f58e95811e5ed7d588901d1efd91.text:
## Durable, Temporal, and Social Knowledge Infrastructures

This community studies how digital information can be modeled, published, preserved, discovered, and reused over time. Major themes include web archiving and temporal access; digital-object repositories and preservation architectures; semantic and linked-data publication; scholarly communication, provenance, and citation; annotations and manuscript data; and social tagging, recommendation, and information diffusion.

Typical methods combine standards-based system design with empirical evaluation. Papers develop RDF/ontology models, nanopublications, provenance and versioning mechanisms, persistent identifiers, OAI-PMH, ResourceSync, Memento, Fedora, and Open Annotation infrastructures. Web-archive research uses focused and event-driven crawling, archive graphs, cache and coverage analysis, temporal ranking, rediscovery of missing pages, and coherence or drift measurements. Scholarly-data work applies metadata aggregation, entity linking, claim and citation extraction, and bibliometric analysis. Social systems use cognitive models of frequency, recency, memory, semantic context, trust, and attention, alongside collaborative filtering, classifiers, deep learning, and learning-to-rank.

Recent directions emphasize large-scale and durable temporal knowledge: diachronic linked data, persistent annotations, decentralized publication, human-assisted preservation, semantic search layers over archives, and scalable archive analytics. Recommendation research increasingly addresses cold starts, novelty, salience, and realistic folksonomy structure, while preservation work focuses on web change, synchronization, format migration, and long-term scholarly reproducibility.

titles<=300|778d02e06c9a0f147744eb6a8806.text:
## Graph Data Management, Querying, and Scalable Knowledge Graphs

This community centers on foundations and implementation of graph data management, especially SPARQL over RDF and federated or distributed repositories. Major themes include SPARQL semantics, satisfiability, multiset and negation behavior, query optimization, provenance, updates, views, completeness, and reasoning over OWL/RDFS. A parallel focus is navigational querying: regular and context-free path queries, reachability, shortest paths, traversal languages, and expressive-power and complexity analyses.

Typical methods combine formal language and database theory with practical systems research. Papers develop cost-based and heuristic query reordering, join-size estimation, indexes and reachability oracles, compressed storage, incremental view maintenance, matrix multiplication, MapReduce/Spark/HBase execution, and adaptive partitioning. Benchmarking and workload generation are prominent through systems such as gMark, SP2Bench, Geographica, and BigDataBench.

The collection also connects RDF with property graphs, XML, relational databases, and linked-data interfaces. Emerging directions include streaming and temporal graphs, historical graph analytics, visual and example-based querying, schema and shape languages, annotated and uncertain data, privacy-preserving graph analysis, and entity linking. Federated querying increasingly addresses replicated, divergent, heterogeneous, and web-scale data sources, while graph view maintenance and provenance support more dynamic and explainable systems.

titles<=300|63d1c44e5dc3c7d9b2410858c34e.text:
### Scalable, Adaptive Data Management and Analytics
