Major themes include consensus and disagreement, polarization, structural balance in signed trust–mistrust networks, homophily, community identity, bounded confidence, stubborn agents, susceptibility, biased assimilation, and heterogeneous thresholds. Several works examine interconnected topics, private versus expressed opinions, social biases, and the feedback between opinion formation and personalized recommendations.

Typical methods combine dynamical-systems and graph-theoretic analysis with stochastic and Markovian models, threshold and bounded-confidence processes, Friedkin–Johnsen and DeGroot–Friedkin frameworks, weighted-median influence, fluid approximations, and asymptotic convergence analysis. Researchers also address identification, influence estimation from partial observations, distributed inference, active and interactive sensing, diffusion control, and removal of data incest.

The community increasingly emphasizes dynamic, random, and signed network topologies, including state- and relative-state-flipping models, time-varying interaction matrices, and social balance evolution. Applications extend to YouTube engagement and popularity forecasting, online collective behavior, political discourse, and knowledge segregation. A growing direction integrates network dynamics with decision making, recommendation systems, and interventions designed to regulate polarization, diffusion, or social dominance.

titles<=300|abbaf254f8dfeb95c6862066ed39.text:
### Community Report: Fair Search, Social Information Systems, and Scalable Data Retrieval

This community studies information discovery across web, social, professional, and bibliographic environments. Major themes include search and recommendation quality, fairness and diversity in ranked results, collaborative information seeking, expert and talent discovery, and semantic enrichment using Wikipedia, Wiktionary, WordNet, ontologies, and linked data. Collaborative tagging and folksonomies are analyzed as evolving social and semantic networks, including vocabulary growth, influence, attention, expertise, and user behavior.

A substantial database strand addresses top-*k*, skyline, preference, fuzzy, incomplete, and aggregate queries over relational, XML, hidden-web, streaming, spatial, and graph data. Other work targets approximate nearest-neighbor and similarity search, query planning, indexing, distributed and peer-to-peer retrieval, and efficient crawling of hidden databases.

Typical methods include learning-to-rank, query expansion and reranking, entity linking and disambiguation, semantic and ontology matching, graph analysis, clustering, game-theoretic and agent-based models, factorization and hashing, GPU acceleration, and randomized preference collection. Evaluation relies on retrieval metrics, representative query samples, user studies, click logs, and demographic audits.

Recent directions emphasize algorithmic fairness—exposure, attention, disparate satisfaction, and ranking quality—alongside diversity-aware recommendation and antidote data. The literature also moves toward deep ranking, federated and personalized search, multilingual entity ranking, real-time social-media analysis, and scalable graph-based retrieval.

titles<=300|2bb75bf0adee98fad12ffcd40e7e.text:
## Spatial Networks, Modularity, and Social Influence

This community studies how network structure, geography, and indirect relationships shape clustering and influence. A central theme is community detection: extending modularity with distance-based null models, finding spatially near or geographically dispersed communities, and developing latent parameter node-centric models for spatial networks. Several papers examine the theory and computation of modularity, including the stability of the PWP method, the hardness of bipartite modularity maximization, additive approximation algorithms, and theoretical limits of modularity-based clustering.

A second theme concerns indirect influence. The work develops methods for ranking and deconstructing influence links and applies these ideas to international trade. Related research investigates influence diffusion, including targeting large social networks for viral marketing with small seed sets.

Applications emphasize security and political violence. Studies address the diffusion and permeability of violence across borders in North and West Africa, early identification of violent gang members, and social-network intelligence for combating street-gang violence.

Overall, the papers trend from foundational analyses of modularity, stability, and computational complexity toward geographically informed network models and operational applications in influence maximization, violence monitoring, and intelligence analysis.

titles<=300|c3343d383437c9c93cfb79bf49f0.text:
### Networked Analysis for Social Media, Health, and Retrieval

This community centers on applying network science and machine learning to large, heterogeneous information sources. Major themes include social-media analysis—attitudes toward China on Twitter, illicit drug activity and drug reactions on Instagram, public-health image analysis, and hashtag-centered search—as well as recommendation, including Pinterest-to-Twitter board recommendation and semi-metric document networks.

Health and biomedical applications are prominent: studies examine drug–drug interactions in Instagram timelines and electronic health records, including gender and age biases, while protein interactions are extracted from abstracts and text. Information retrieval is addressed through digital-archive search and methods for comparing search-engine rankings.

Typical methods construct and analyze graphs, including complex-network distance closures, semi-metric networks, word-proximity networks, and network-based ranking or recommendation. Other approaches use multimodal image analysis, linear models, guided self-organization inspired by T-cell cross-regulation, and biologically motivated distributed designs for adaptive knowledge management.

Recent directions emphasize fine-grained and large-scale monitoring of social and health phenomena, richer combinations of text, images, timelines, and records, immersive search experiences, and recommendation systems that exploit nontraditional network geometry. Evaluation and fairness are also emerging concerns, particularly in ranking comparison and detecting demographic bias in clinical decision patterns.

titles<=300|577184231efea183b21e937a1b18.text:
## Semantic Models for Structured Knowledge Access

This community focuses on representing complex information through semantic models, repositories, and knowledgebases. A central theme is the use of semantic modeling to describe mechanisms and other highly structured forms of scientific communication, alongside attention to the practical difficulties and representational limits involved.

The papers also apply these ideas to cultural-heritage and local-history resources. Work on digitized historical newspapers combines text mining with coordinated models and formative user-interface design to improve access. Related efforts explore repositories with direct representation and an interactive directory for Norfolk, Nebraska, in 1899–1900.

Typical methods include designing formal semantic representations, organizing information in repositories and knowledgebases, mining textual collections, and developing or evaluating interactive interfaces. The set suggests a movement from abstract modeling toward usable systems that connect structured representations with real-world archival and scientific materials. Recent directions emphasize richer semantic models, direct representation, domain-specific knowledgebases, and interactive access to digitized sources.

titles<=300|dbef65af5b87e596233b5d7a543c.text:
## Utility-C and Constraint-Aware Sequence Mining

This community centers on discovering valuable structure in event and sequence data rather than relying on frequency alone. Core themes include high-utility episodes, utility-oriented and trend mining, sequential patterns, association rules, and compact representations such as closed, non-derivable, generic-base, and compressing episodes.

Typical methods develop specialized search and pruning strategies for serial episodes, simultaneous events, subsequence constraints, complex sequences, and individualized or item-specific minimum-utility thresholds. Projection-based mining is represented by ProUM, while episode screening uses a dual-partition model. Statistical significance assessment complements traditional rule discovery.

The work also broadens the data and system settings: multidimensional and multiple sequences, uncertain data, privacy-preserving mining, and parallel or MapReduce computation. DESQ addresses constrained frequent sequence mining, and n-gram statistics illustrate distributed sequence analytics.

Recent directions emphasize practical utility and scalability: moving beyond frequency, accommodating heterogeneous thresholds and uncertainty, extracting trends for intelligent systems, and processing increasingly complex or distributed sequence collections. At the same time, compression, formal bases, significance testing, and free-rider screening seek to make discovered patterns more concise, interpretable, reliable, and resistant to misleading or redundant results.

titles<=300|9eda29ab888684c24cdb4016ce88.text:
## Algebraic Foundations and High-Performance Polystore Analytics

This community explores scalable data management across relational, NoSQL, graph, array, tensor, and semi-structured systems. A central theme is unification: associative arrays, LARA, relational lattices, relational algebra, and tensor models provide mathematical foundations for databases, matrices, graphs, spreadsheets, and polystores. Query research covers SQL extensions, JSON and MongoDB languages, visual web wrappers, tree queries, conjunctive queries, guarded negation, and monadic Datalog, often emphasizing expressiveness, semantics, and schema specification.

Systems work targets high-throughput ingestion and computation. Accumulo and D4M support large-scale inserts, provenance, cyber-data pipelines, and database operations; Graphulo brings server-side sparse matrix multiplication and graph algorithms to Bigtable-style databases. BigDAWG develops a polystore architecture with relational, array, and tensor abstractions, while Apache Calcite addresses optimized queries over heterogeneous sources. SciDB, Vertica, Laradb, Supercloud, and large-scale ETL systems broaden the platform landscape.

Typical methods include formal proofs and lower bounds, algebraic specification, system architecture and implementation, benchmarking, and domain demonstrations such as pathogen identification and social-network analysis. Recent trends emphasize integrated polystore querying, heterogeneous data models, server-side graph processing, provenance, cloud/HPC scalability, and increasingly configurable SQL and semi-structured data support.

titles<=300|76509e9d2be5c76a3199bf11cba0.text:
## Dynamic Topics, Social Sensing, and Scholarly Recommendation

This community centers on mining evolving text and social-media streams for topics, events, opinions, and actionable knowledge. Major applications include disease surveillance and forecasting, disaster response, political and public sentiment analysis, news monitoring, tourism, and online-community studies. A parallel research line addresses scholarly information extraction, citation and text-reuse analysis, hypothesis generation, knowledge-graph construction, and research-paper recommendation.

Typical methods include LDA and its extensions—hierarchical, dynamic, author-topic, coupled, constrained, limited-attention, and embedding-space models—alongside Bayesian nonparametric processes, matrix/tensor factorization, latent-space and graph-based community models, and probabilistic logical reasoning. Event detection commonly combines temporal or geospatial modeling, interaction graphs, power-law verification, incremental learning, semantic filtering, and summarization. Recommender studies use collaborative/content-based filtering, latent factors, topic regression, user modeling, ranking analysis, and meta-learning for algorithm selection.

Recent directions emphasize scalable and online processing with Hadoop, Spark, and inference-as-a-service architectures; neural embeddings and deep learning for clustering, indexing, and representation; real-time disease and breaking-news detection; cross-source alignment of news, Twitter, and knowledge graphs; and stronger evaluation of recommender quality, ranking bias, dataset persistence, and scientific-output validity.

titles<=300|aa21ef319f8644b3fb3610f6304c.text:
## Dynamic, Temporal, and Multilayer Graph Analysis

This community studies efficient analysis of large, evolving, and richly structured networks. A major theme is graph querying: shortest-path and distance computation, reachability, latency, and point-to-point queries, including dynamic and distributed settings. Methods include landmark labeling, hop doubling, distance sketches, pruning, hubs, indexing, oracles, vertex-centric computation, and performance-guaranteed distributed algorithms.

A second theme concerns temporal and multilayer networks. Stream graphs, link streams, time-varying graphs, and temporal quantities support the analysis of interactions, paths, centrality, indicators, and layer structure. Algebraic and semiring-based approaches, time-series analysis, and temporal query processing provide formal tools for reasoning about time and order. Window analytics and order-enforcement optimization address practical processing over dynamic data.

Applications focus on social and information systems: opinion spreading and monopolies, media power and gossip, trust-aware and movie recommendation, scientific-network selection and emergence, mailing-list discussions, and hospital contacts. Movie scripts and ratings are modeled with multilayer or link-stream features.

Recent trends emphasize scalable indexing and distributed execution, exact yet fast distance algorithms, principled temporal abstractions, and integration of structural, temporal, textual, and sentiment signals for network-based prediction.

titles<=300|63137939c6b363a402020c36a8d2.text:
**Geometry, Generation, and Dynamics in Complex Networks**

This community studies how network structure can be modeled, generated, and exploited. A central theme is geometric and hyperbolic organization: geometric inhomogeneous random graphs and replaying hyperbolic growth are used to explain or reproduce network maps. Several works focus on controllable graph synthesis, including methods for generating connected random graphs and constructing constrained graphs through multiple edge switches.

The papers also examine how structural properties affect network behavior and algorithms. “Super blockers” investigates the influence of network structure on information cascades, while work on greedy routing explores how local geometric structure can produce algorithmic small-world behavior.

Typical methods combine random-graph models, geometric or hyperbolic embeddings, growth-process replay, edge-switching procedures, and algorithmic analyses of routing and diffusion. Overall, the research trends toward structure-aware network generation: preserving connectivity or other constraints while retaining meaningful topology, and linking those structural choices to navigability and cascade dynamics.

titles<=300|75d1700e245a8ad6963a2544a4ef.text:
## Information Retrieval: Neural Ranking, Search Context, and Reliable Evaluation

This community centers on information retrieval and ranking across web, enterprise, mobile, biomedical, e-commerce, social-media, and conversational settings. Major themes include neural relevance modeling, passage and document retrieval, query understanding and expansion, entity- and knowledge-graph search, personalization, table and dataset search, question answering, and multimedia retrieval.

Typical methods combine learning-to-rank—including pairwise, listwise, groupwise, counterfactual, and online approaches—with deep interaction models such as BERT, Duet, PACRR, convolutional and recurrent networks, attention, kernel pooling, and reinforcement learning. Embeddings, semantic hashing, approximate-nearest-neighbor graphs, weak supervision, pseudo-relevance feedback, and entity linking support scalable matching and retrieval. Evaluation is addressed through ranking metrics, unbiased click modeling, multileaving, bandits, online experimentation, robustness analysis, and reproducibility tooling.

Recent work emphasizes contextual and conversational search, neural re-ranking and semantic matching, domain adaptation, explainability, and fairness or bias correction in feedback. E-commerce search increasingly incorporates user intent, product neighborhoods, task models, and online optimization. Other growing directions include retrieval over tables and data lakes, knowledge-grounded question answering, personalized recommendations, and efficient production-scale indexing and inference.

titles<=300|b359259f69742904b56dc3af14e5.text:
## Natural-Language and Online Access to Scientific Databases

This community focuses on making large, structured scientific datasets accessible through natural-language and web-based interfaces. A central theme is translating business, biological, and general user questions into SQL, while addressing the semantic gap between user language and database schemas. Related work explores knowledge-rich querying, queried units, entity-graph preview tables, and surveys of natural-language database interfaces.

Typical methods include SQL generation from natural-language requests, learning from SQL query logs, end-to-end neural interfaces, and structured representations that expose database entities and units. Several systems emphasize practical data access: SkyServer and AstroServ support astronomical data discovery and serving across the data life cycle, while the World Wide Telescope illustrates an online science environment. Cloud-based, real-time, low-latency event analysis extends these ideas to streaming scientific workloads.

Recent trends move from manually designed interfaces toward learned and neural query generation, richer semantic and knowledge-aware representations, and interactive previews. At the infrastructure level, the work increasingly addresses distributed, cloud-based, real-time analysis of large-scale scientific data, while maintaining usability for nonexpert users.

titles<=300|a4313f3f7f0e9964f92781c1b636.text:
## Information Retrieval: Neural Ranking, Context, and Search Applications

This community centers on information retrieval and ranking across web, enterprise, academic, biomedical, e-commerce, social-media, and mobile settings. Major themes include document, passage, answer, entity, table, image, and product retrieval; query understanding, expansion, reformulation, and intent detection; personalization and conversational search; and dataset, expertise, and knowledge-graph search.

Typical methods combine learning-to-rank with neural representations and interaction models, including BERT, convolutional/recurrent networks, attention, kernel pooling, dual and multi-resolution embeddings, listwise/groupwise scoring, and reinforcement learning. Graph embeddings, metapaths, entity linking, semantic hashing, locality-sensitive hashing, inverted indexes, and approximate-nearest-neighbor graphs support representation and scalable retrieval. Weak supervision, pseudo-relevance feedback, click and activity logs, and question-answer data are common training signals.

Recent work emphasizes deep and contextual reranking, passage and non-factoid QA, table-based answering, conversational and session search, and entity-oriented retrieval. Strong growth appears in unbiased and counterfactual online learning-to-rank, propensity correction, multileaving, bandit evaluation, and reliable experimentation. Other emerging directions include explainable and interpretable neural retrieval, adversarial robustness, domain adaptation, privacy-preserving model sharing, efficient indexing, and applications of search data to event, health, and public-information monitoring.

titles<=300|8493f88b657f3b7d0d8f84d0ac4f.text:
### Acknowledgements as Data for Mapping Research Collaboration

This community studies acknowledgements as an underused source for understanding research funding, collaboration, and leadership across disciplines. One major theme is the characterization of funding-acknowledgement data in Web of Science, including its potential uses, limitations, and interpretation caveats. Complementary work develops queries for extracting and analyzing funding acknowledgements while emphasizing methodological caution.

Several papers extend acknowledgement analysis beyond funding. Humanities research uses acknowledgements to make otherwise invisible contributions and relationships visible, while another study combines authorship and acknowledgements to reveal broader collaboration patterns. Research leadership and collaboration-network studies examine how leadership flows are shaped by proximity and network structure.

Typical methods include bibliographic and Web of Science data analysis, acknowledgement querying and classification, network analysis, and the integration of authorship with acknowledgement information. The recent trend is toward combining traditionally separate research indicators: funding records, authorship, acknowledgements, collaboration networks, and proximity. Overall, the literature positions acknowledgements as valuable complementary evidence, while stressing careful data interpretation and awareness of coverage and query-related limitations.

titles<=300|46ab7f4042fabce3f85580ad783e.text:
## Dynamic Graph Algorithms and Temporal Social Networks

This community centers on efficient analysis of large, dynamic, and temporal graphs. A major theme is distance and reachability querying, including shortest paths, point-to-point distances, single-source queries, reachability oracles, labeling schemes, distance sketches, and distributed query processing. Methods emphasize pruning, hubs, landmarks, hop doubling, indexing, vertex-centric computation, and provable or performance guarantees.

A second theme develops formal models for interactions over time: temporal and time-varying graphs, link and stream graphs, multilayer networks, weighted or directed streams, and algebraic or semiring-based temporal analysis. Proposed measures include temporal indicators, latencies, centralities, and layer centralities, with applications to hospitals, mailing lists, knowledge mobilization, and social interaction.

The community also applies network structure to narrative and cultural data, including fictional-character extraction, movie scripts, books, television plots, *Friends*, *Game of Thrones*, and film cast sizes. Typical tasks include genre classification, kill prediction, narrative smoothing, and comparing extraction techniques.

Additional applications cover opinions, trust, cryptocurrency trading, recommendations, sentiment, and scientific networks. Recent trends favor scalable processing of dynamic graphs, window analytics, temporal recommendations, multilayer representations, and combining graph structure with content or learning-based signals.

titles<=300|abcf4746de14392fda4d0e1384ac.text:
## Social Media Mining, Network Analysis, and Recommendation

This community focuses on extracting social, geographic, semantic, and health-related signals from online platforms and text collections. Major themes include identifying gang members and illicit drug activity on Twitter and Instagram; analyzing attitudes, social identity, cohesion, expertise, and music sentiment; and studying public-health issues such as drug interactions, reactions, and demographic bias in electronic health records.

Typical methods combine network analysis, word and spatio-temporal embeddings, multimodal image and text analysis, sentiment trajectories, semantic place descriptors, and proximity-based text networks. Recommender-system research explores Pinterest–Twitter transfer, point-of-interest ranking, semi-metric networks, and document-network structure. Other work addresses guided self-organization, adaptive knowledge management, digital-archive search, hashtag-centered immersive search, and comparison of search-engine rankings.

Recent directions emphasize fine-grained and multimodal social-media analysis, unsupervised representation learning for users and locations, geo-temporal sequential ranking, and network-based monitoring of health and illicit behavior. Across applications, the papers increasingly connect large-scale behavioral data with interpretable social, spatial, and biomedical relationships.

titles<=300|934c6386f6664d86dad58a4a5bf4.text:
### Ontology-Driven Semantic Information Retrieval

This community focuses on improving text and semantic search by enriching conventional keyword retrieval with ontological knowledge. Core themes include representing documents and queries through ontological features, named entities, WordNet concepts, and latent semantic or ontological relationships.

Typical methods combine keywords with ontology-derived features, apply query expansion using related or latent named entities, and use spreading activation to propagate relevance through ontology structures. The generalized vector space model provides a framework for incorporating ontology-based representations into retrieval, while other approaches emphasize semantic search through activation-based reasoning or latent ontological features.

Recent work trends toward increasingly implicit and relational representations. Rather than relying only on explicit ontology matches, newer approaches identify latent relationships among named entities and ontological features, enabling broader query interpretation. Overall, the papers show a progression from combining surface terms with structured ontological information toward integrated semantic models that support query-oriented expansion, relevance propagation, and latent concept discovery.

titles<=300|569b1daced39f62596221ab27d87.text:
## Social, Semantic, and Geo-Temporal Recommendation

This community studies recommendation, search, and classification in socially generated and location-aware data. A major theme is cognitive and semantic modeling of social tagging: frequency, recency, forgetting, semantic context, memory activation, and social cues are used to improve tag reuse and recommendation. Other work develops social recommenders for online marketplaces, Pinterest, points of interest, jobs, researchers, and sparse or cold-start settings, incorporating trust, social identity, cohesion, attention, novelty, coverage, and item embeddings.

Typical methods include collaborative filtering, regular equivalence, graph and link analysis, semi-metric networks, random surfing, topic modeling, word and spatio-temporal embeddings, sparse additive generative models, and biologically inspired distributed or self-organizing models. The community also addresses scalable retrieval through streaming similarity joins, similarity search, ranking comparison, and digital-archive mining.

Recent directions emphasize multimodal and geo-temporal social-media analysis, including illicit drug monitoring, public-health imagery, health-record bias, and fine-grained Twitter attitude or community analysis. Researchers increasingly combine semantic, temporal, spatial, and network signals, while evaluating recommendation trade-offs beyond accuracy and examining confirmation bias, trust, social influence, and the representation of expertise and interests.

titles<=300|01e5ceded4849dc3d03a7d214234.text:
## Software, Data, and Reproducibility in Research

This community examines how software and data function as scholarly research objects and how their contributions can be recognized, documented, and sustained. Core themes include software and dependency representation in citation graphs, academic data-sharing practices, software and data citation through Zenodo DOIs, and the measurement of software impact—illustrated by an examination of the `lme4` R package.

The papers use empirical surveys, citation-graph analysis, citation tracking, case-based examination, and journal review. Conceptual work on reproducibility terminology complements studies of infrastructure and scholarly practice. The Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS) and the ReScience initiative represent publication and sustainability models intended to support reusable, verifiable computational research.

Recent trends emphasize formalizing terminology, assigning persistent identifiers to software and data, integrating these objects into citation systems, and developing more reliable measures of software impact. Overall, the community moves beyond viewing software as merely a tool toward treating software, data, and reproducibility practices as first-class components of scholarly communication.

titles<=300|02ada99d2fa0e98ca6af900d0745.text:
## Community Report: Semantic Search Meets Scalable Data Systems

This community combines three major themes. First, it studies text classification and clustering, including multinomial mixtures, topic models, association rules, nearest-neighbor and medoid methods, Bayesian models, semantic relations, ontologies, feature selection, and evolutionary optimization. Applications include authorship attribution, opinion-spam and sentiment detection, hierarchical categorization, and personalized search.

Second, a substantial body of work targets mathematical information retrieval and knowledge management. Projects address formula repositories, formula embeddings, context-aware representations, mathematical language processing, equation-aware topic models, rendering, search evaluation, question answering, and semantic mappings between computer-algebra and document systems.

Third, the community develops scalable data infrastructure. Associative arrays, relational and tensor algebras, lattices, and sparse matrices provide common abstractions for databases and graphs. Systems such as D4M, Accumulo, Graphulo, BigDAWG, SciDB, Calcite, Vertica, and Supercloud support polystore queries, graph analytics, provenance, ingestion, and high-throughput pipelines.

Typical methods include machine learning, similarity and edit-distance measures, semantic annotation, benchmarking, algebraic modeling, and distributed database optimization. Recent trends emphasize billion-scale updates, dynamic scaling, on-demand computing, heterogeneous data integration, server-side graph processing, and increasingly context- and formula-aware semantic search.

titles<=300|200a78929af1181699098a9a1b64.text:
## Social, Cognitive, and Streaming Recommendation

This community studies recommendation in socially connected, sparse, and rapidly changing environments. A major theme is social tagging and hashtag recommendation: papers model cognitive processes, memory activation and forgetting, frequency, recency, semantic context, and temporal reuse. Other work examines confirmation bias and whether users are influenced more by friends or crowds.

Recommendation research also incorporates social-network, trust, geographic, sentiment, and marketplace signals for products, categories, jobs, and resources. Methods include collaborative filtering, regular equivalence for trust-based cold-start handling, sparse additive generative models, hybrid attention-inspired recommenders, social recommender engines, and deep learning for large-scale cold-start problems. Item embeddings are evaluated beyond accuracy, including their value for student-job matching. Long-tail recommendation and sparsity remain central concerns.

A parallel stream addresses graph and data-stream computation, including link analysis on bipartite graphs, random surfing without teleportation, rumor-dissemination models, and top-*k* similarity joins and self-joins over endless or set streams.

Recent trends move toward cognitively informed temporal models, multimodal contextual signals such as location and sentiment, scalable streaming algorithms, and richer evaluations that consider user behavior, social influence, and practical value rather than accuracy alone.

titles<=300|d47ad3455f9eb2a8acffde6d1c5c.text:
### Utility-Oriented Sequential and Pattern Mining

This community focuses on extending pattern mining beyond frequency toward **utility, value, and actionable significance**. Major themes include high-utility itemsets, episodes, sequences, trends, and revenue-maximizing recommendations, with applications to intelligent systems and social content.

Typical methods include **utility-driven and projection-based mining**, discovery of high-utility episodes, mining under varied or individualized minimum-utility thresholds, and analysis across multiple or uncertain sequences. Researchers emphasize compact representations and efficient outputs through **closed episodes, strict episodes, compressing serial episodes, generic association-rule bases, and non-derivable frequent itemsets**. Subsequence constraints and simultaneous events are also incorporated into sequential mining.

A parallel methodological strand addresses **scalability and distributed computation**, including parallel sequential pattern mining, MapReduce-based social-content matching, and n-gram statistics. Other work considers the reliability and governance of discovered patterns through privacy-preserving utility mining, statistical significance assessment, and free-rider episode screening.

Recent trends move toward practical, context-sensitive analytics: optimizing revenue, handling uncertainty, assigning item- or user-specific thresholds, exploiting distributed infrastructures, and integrating utility with trend discovery and recommendation.

titles<=300|27867b7063735e9bc02ea43febad.text:
### Graph Representation Learning for Dynamic and Heterogeneous Networks

This community focuses on learning, analyzing, and generating representations of large, evolving, and richly attributed graphs. Major themes include node and network embeddings, link prediction, community detection, role identification, graph similarity, alignment, and influence estimation. Applications span social networks, recommender systems, fraud and money-laundering detection, citation and knowledge graphs, online behavior, and financial networks.

Typical methods combine random walks (DeepWalk, node2vec, struc2vec), matrix factorization, spectral techniques, latent-space and stochastic block models, graph sampling, motif and triangle counting, and graph neural networks. Heterogeneous settings use metapaths, relational attention, multimodal features, text, and knowledge bases. Dynamic-network studies model temporal motifs, event graphs, change points, evolving communities, and time-aware embeddings for prediction and anomaly detection.

Recent work increasingly emphasizes temporal robustness, scalable and streaming computation, higher-order and multilayer structure, and representations preserving both local and global information. Adversarial attacks and defenses, privacy, uncertainty, missing links, and evaluation reliability are growing concerns. Generative graph models, graph alignment, and application-oriented systems for recommendation, cybersecurity, scholarly mining, and financial forensics also appear prominently.

titles<=300|ae02f5466f2e84cf8a3664eabfd3.text:
## Search, Semantics, and Social Web Intelligence

This community investigates information retrieval across search engines, libraries, Wikipedia, Wiktionary, folksonomies, and professional networks. Major themes include ranking and entity retrieval, query expansion and related-term search, ontology matching, multilingual linking, semantic navigation, and evaluation of search quality. A parallel focus examines collaborative tagging: vocabulary growth, tag hierarchies, reuse, expertise, attention, and the structure of tagging communities.

Typical methods combine relational, XML, and wiki-index database systems with graph and complex-network analysis. Researchers use PageRank-like ranking, centrality and local-dimension measures, clustering, power-law analysis, and agent-based modeling to identify influential users and understand information diffusion. Retrieval studies employ representative query samples, relevance judgments, clickthrough logs, user experiments, and statistical modeling. Machine learning supports topic selection, personalized search, talent recommendation, entity disambiguation, and learning to rank.

Recent work emphasizes deep ranking for search verticals, featured snippets, fair Wikipedia ranking, global multilingual entity ranking, and large-scale expertise mining. Professional-network studies increasingly address personalized federated search, candidate and job recommendation, talent flows, and preference prediction. Microblog research analyzes hot-event discussion, user behavior, attention, influence, and location forecasting, while social tagging research continues toward semantic interoperability and collective knowledge organization.

titles<=300|6e7307df8143773b0d6073d9a812.text:
### Energy-Aware and Resource-Adaptive Distributed Databases

This community investigates how distributed database architecture, workload management, and data placement affect both performance and energy consumption. A central theme is energy-efficient database and cluster design, including comparisons of database operations under different workload scenarios and evaluations of whether clusters of low-power (“wimpy”) nodes can compete with powerful (“brawny”) servers.

The papers emphasize autonomic, resource-aware systems that dynamically respond to available computing resources. Dynamic physiological partitioning is explored for shared-nothing clusters, while workstation- and cluster-based distributed database architectures target adaptive resource use.

Data locality is another major focus. Methods include data placement and replica selection to improve co-location in distributed environments, as well as graph partitioning for distributed placement. These approaches connect placement decisions with communication costs, cluster utilization, and efficiency.

Overall, the research trends from isolated performance or architecture questions toward integrated, eco-friendly database management. Recent directions emphasize combining workload-aware optimization, autonomic adaptation, dynamic partitioning, and graph-based placement to balance performance, scalability, and energy efficiency across heterogeneous distributed systems.

titles<=300|3de461f3e6367cbd755c9b892197.text:
**Socioeconomic Inference from Digital Social Networks**

This community studies how socioeconomic structure and demographic attributes are reflected in large-scale digital communication and consumption networks. A central theme is the discovery of correlations and stratification: consumption patterns are analyzed across social-economic networks, including their temporal dynamics, while communication networks are examined for socioeconomic correlations.

The papers also investigate inference of individual attributes from online behavior. Twitter-based studies estimate users’ ages and socioeconomic status, using signals related to location, occupation, and language or semantics. Together, these works treat social-media activity and communication behavior as indirect measurements of population characteristics.

Typical methods include statistical analysis of network properties, correlation analysis, temporal/dynamic modeling, and feature-based prediction from user-generated information and network context. The comparative study of large mobile-phone calling networks broadens the empirical basis beyond Twitter and emphasizes cross-network regularities.

A notable trend is the movement from describing aggregate network statistics toward modeling dynamic consumption relationships and inferring demographic or socioeconomic attributes at the user level. Across the community, digital traces are increasingly used to study social inequality, population segmentation, and the relationship between communication behavior and socioeconomic position.

titles<=300|d9022c29e7991381a118bb2c9e79.text:
## Network Centrality, Wikipedia Mining, and Large-Scale Social Systems

This community centers on ranking, centrality, and network structure, especially for directed, weighted, incomplete, evolving, and massive graphs. A major theme is the theory and evaluation of PageRank and related measures: stability, axiomatic foundations, discriminating power, uncertainty, localization, normalization, subgraph centrality, total communicability, current-flow and randomized-shortest-path betweenness, and node criticality. Practical work develops scalable random-walk-with-restart, top-*k*, node-discovery, accessibility, backbone, coverage, navigation, and spectral-radius-reduction algorithms.

Wikipedia and DBLP provide central empirical settings. Reduced Google matrices, multilingual rankings, Wikidata, biographical links, and editor-interaction networks are used to study geopolitical ties, cultures, universities, scientific communities, terrorism, gender inequality, political leaders, and historical influence. Other studies analyze Twitter, petitions, social games, Foursquare, Bitcoin, urban streets, and epidemic networks.

Typical methods include Google-matrix and spectral analysis, random walks, graphons, matrix factorization, block-matrix formulations, clustering, sampling, optimization, genetic algorithms, and temporal network analysis. Text-focused papers apply lexical chains, semantic and sentiment features, WordNet/Wikipedia knowledge, and learning-to-rank for summarization and news detection.

Recent directions emphasize billion-scale approximate computation, dynamic and incomplete networks, network design for influence or epidemic control, cultural and gender-aware analyses, and interpretable mining of large online knowledge and social systems.

titles<=300|692f066607c6adca552ef5296b92.text:
## Scholarly Information Extraction and Recommendation

This community focuses on improving scholarly search, discovery, and research assessment through two connected themes: extracting structured knowledge from scientific literature and using it to power recommender systems. Work on metadata, author contributions, OCR, citation and reference parsing, citation matching, and semantic publishing supports interlinked scholarly knowledge graphs, including the ACL Anthology Knowledge Graph Miner.

A second major theme is academic recommendation: related-article and repository recommenders, recommender APIs and services, mind-map-based user modeling, and large-scale resources such as the 94-million-item RARD II dataset. Studies examine practical deployment challenges, choice overload, position bias, citation reuse, and the effects of time, ranking randomization, and social signals such as Twitter followers. Evaluation also compares expert, search-engine, and recommender rankings.

Typical methods combine information extraction, rules and machine learning, meta-learning for parser selection, citation and bibliographic analysis, user studies, ranking experiments, and distributed processing with Apache Hadoop. Recent directions emphasize scalable, operational recommender platforms; robust, retrained parsing models; semantic interlinking and quality assessment; richer personalization; and evaluation protocols that account for temporal effects and user behavior.

titles<=300|ff03138ebb3778ac701870c0e5a2.text:
## Text Classification and Math-Aware Information Retrieval

This community centers on machine learning for text classification, clustering, and semantic search, with a distinctive emphasis on mathematical information. Research addresses authorship attribution, opinion-spam and sentiment detection, hierarchical and skewed classification, subject indexing, document-type recognition, and personalized content customization. Mathematical information retrieval spans formula repositories, notation namespaces, formula rendering and conversion, math-aware search engines, query-result merging, and question answering.

Typical methods include multinomial mixture models, naïve Bayes, k-nearest neighbors, k-medoids, association rules, term-class relevance measures, similarity search, vector-based evaluation, semantic relations, ontologies, Wikitology, and feature selection. Hierarchical classification uses route-confidence estimation and horizontal/vertical separation; clustering and topic models support corpus analysis, visualization, and topical-diversity measurement. Graph and edit-distance methods appear in image classification, node metrics, and tree comparison. Evolutionary and genetic algorithms optimize keywords, navigation, and adaptive retrieval.

Recent work trends toward semantic and context-aware representations, scalable mathematical search, integration of text with formulas, and improved access to digital mathematical libraries and Wikipedia. Social-media analysis, multilingual classification, web-page segmentation, and machine-learning-based opinion and sentiment analysis broaden the application scope.

titles<=300|fccecd6302c772ceb1598bc579c7.text:
### Community Report: Semantic Search, Evaluation, and Knowledge Organization

This community centers on improving information access through structured knowledge, search evaluation, and personalization. A major theme is the transformation and exploitation of Wikipedia, Wiktionary, WordNet, folksonomies, and classification systems such as UDC. Papers study ontology matching, thesaurus construction, category hierarchies, semantic navigation, multilingual entity linking, and global entity ranking.

Search-engine research addresses retrieval effectiveness, relevance and credibility, query expansion, navigational and foreign-language queries, result descriptions, commercial intent, featured snippets, and fairness in ranking. Evaluation methods include representative query sampling, shallow versus deep judging, click-through preference collection, assessor and user studies, and analyses of search effort, difficulty, and demographic effects.

Typical technical approaches combine relational or native XML databases with indexing, graph algorithms, PageRank approximations, learning-to-rank, deep ranking models, and network analysis. Social and professional search is prominent, including expertise recommendation, talent discovery, personalized and federated search, influence detection, and modeling talent flows.

Recent directions emphasize multilingual and cross-source entity resolution, large-scale mining of experts and communities, personalized ranking, unbiased preference estimation, and deployment of deep models in search verticals. Overall, the community links semantic knowledge organization with empirical evaluation and increasingly personalized, graph-based search systems.

titles<=300|e2a8c3084b2b4d5e22d0a9e32ac6.text:
## Network Science for Knowledge, Influence, and Culture

This community studies large-scale networks as models of knowledge, society, and narrative. Wikipedia and Wikidata are central: papers analyze multilingual link structures, cultural and geopolitical relations, biographies, universities, literature, gender bias, editing conflicts, completeness, and the growth of language editions. Related work examines Twitter, Facebook, petitions, online collaboration, street networks, migration, scientific careers, movies, television, and fictional characters.

A major methodological theme is ranking and centrality. PageRank, Google matrices, CheiRank, 2DRank, Katz, betweenness, communicability, navigability, random walks, shortest paths, and flow-based measures are proposed, axiomatized, compared, or optimized. Spectral embeddings, reduced Google matrices, matrix updates, backbone extraction, link prediction, community detection, and influence maximization support analysis of large or incomplete graphs. Diffusion, social learning, random search, immunization, and network games provide dynamic perspectives.

Text mining, natural-language processing, sequence analysis, sentiment features, and machine learning connect graph structure with summarization, political communication, news detection, election prediction, and narrative analysis.

Recent directions emphasize temporal and multilayer networks, multilingual and cross-cultural comparison, knowledge-base quality and class completeness, scalable algorithms, and socially consequential questions around gender, prestige, inequality, participation, and collective memory.

titles<=300|f4e74f84c99912423d0a3d2ce592.text:
### Complex Event Processing for Streaming and IoT

This community centers on **complex event processing (CEP)**: detecting meaningful patterns in high-volume event streams and supporting query and inference over them. Foundational work defines CEP concepts, while SASE provides a stream-oriented processing framework. A major theme is **efficient pattern detection**, including adaptive techniques and **lazy chain automata** for complex event patterns. Another focus is **query optimization**, particularly join optimization for CEP applications.

The papers also address operational challenges in continuous processing. *Consistent Streaming Through Time* emphasizes maintaining coherent stream-processing behavior, while work on **load shedding** considers how to manage overload by reducing processing demands. Applications extend CEP beyond generic streams: a data-centric view of the Internet of Things and distributed inference for **RFID tracking and monitoring** connect event processing with sensor data and physical-world observation.

Overall, the research progresses from foundational models and execution frameworks toward more efficient, adaptive, optimized, and distributed processing. Recent directions emphasize scalable stream handling, specialized automata, consistency over time, and CEP-enabled IoT monitoring.

titles<=300|5d7e5186d6d083c7d19b698a6e27.text:
### Social Networks for Information, Influence, and Marketplace Decisions

This community examines how information and influence propagate through social networks and how these processes shape online-marketplace behavior. Core themes include rumor dissemination, trust and consumer choice, peer versus crowd influence, and social-network support for classifieds and recommendations.

Typical methods range from formal computational modeling with convergence theorems to empirical or system-oriented approaches. The papers consider the “price of trust” in passing shopping information, compare decisions swayed by friends with those shaped by broader crowds, and combine online social-network data with location-based signals to recommend marketplace items. The Serefind system illustrates the practical application of social networking to classified listings.

An apparent recent direction is the movement from abstract modeling of network diffusion toward integrated social-commerce systems. These systems use relational, behavioral, and geographic information to improve recommendations and information exchange, while continuing to investigate how trust, peer influence, and collective signals affect consumer decisions.

titles<=300|237018f840aa57b999e2a5e1ff21.text:
## Scholarly Networks, Bibliometrics, and Enhanced Information Retrieval

This community centers on computational analysis and discovery in scholarly information systems. Major themes include author-name disambiguation and entity matching; coauthorship, citation, and thematic networks; bibliometric indicators of influence, prestige, credit, and performance; and recommendation, expert search, and exploratory retrieval in digital libraries. Additional work addresses knowledge organization, thesauri, terminology mapping, semantic heterogeneity, visualization, and the stewardship and reuse of research data.

Typical methods are graph-based: PageRank and personalized ranking, centrality, community detection, label propagation, stochastic block models, citation-network analysis, and link prediction. Studies also use blocking and deduplication, probabilistic and semi-supervised disambiguation, relative-frequency models, deep neural networks, temporal embeddings, and learning-to-rank. Information retrieval research applies query and term expansion, author or journal recommendations, clustering, graph-based multimedia fusion, and interactive browsing. Evaluation commonly relies on digital-library logs, test collections, surveys, laboratory user studies, and bibliometric comparisons.

Recent trends emphasize scalable analysis of large scholarly and patent networks, dynamic modeling of influence and emerging technologies, machine-learning-based disambiguation and prediction, personalized and context-aware retrieval, interactive visual analytics, and stronger attention to open data, provenance, reproducibility, and research infrastructures.

titles<=300|e00c1f7f3ac7762499f7e6ca8cd1.text:
## Temporal and Dynamic Graph Analytics

This community focuses on modeling, querying, and analyzing networks whose links, vertices, weights, or layers evolve over time. Core themes include temporal reachability, shortest paths, distances, latencies, and centrality, alongside frameworks such as temporal networks, stream graphs, link streams, multilayer stream graphs, and time-varying graphs.

Typical methods emphasize scalable algorithmics and indexing: reachability oracles, landmark labeling, hub acceleration, distributed and vertex-centric computation, graph indexes, and query-plan optimization. Algebraic approaches use temporal quantities and semirings, while window analytics support queries over evolving graphs. Other methodological tools include dynamic graphlets, directed graphlets, network alignment, signal analysis, and labeling schemes for distance queries.

Applications span opinion spreading and dynamic monopolies, media and gossip, hospital contacts, mailing-list threads, cryptocurrency trading, trust-aware recommendation, movie recommendation, and scientific collaboration or selection networks. Several works study temporal indicators, time centrality, and the emergence of structure or algorithmic information.

Recent directions increasingly combine temporal and multilayer representations, scalable exact querying on large dynamic graphs, distributed processing, and recommendation features derived from link streams, sentiment, or temporal interaction patterns.

titles<=300|3f7ae56072626186296aaf766c4b.text:
## Social, Cognitive, and Temporal Recommender Systems

This community studies recommendation in social tagging, online marketplaces, and social networks. A major theme is cognitive modeling of tag reuse and forgetting: frequency, recency, semantic context, memory activation, attention, and confirmation bias are used to explain and improve tag and hashtag recommendations. Work also examines user acceptance, folksonomy structure, and semantic similarity, including e-book annotation and Twitter hashtag reuse.

A second theme is socially informed recommendation. Studies use friendship, crowds, trust, weak ties, regular equivalence, location, and social-network information to recommend products, categories, and marketplace items. Methods include trust-based and social-regularized collaborative filtering, hybrid resource recommenders, scalable social recommender engines, and models addressing cold start and social-commerce behavior.

The community also investigates social information diffusion and influence through rumor dissemination models, convergence analysis, consumer choice, and empirical studies of shopping platforms and classifieds. Typical methods combine computational and cognitive models, online experiments, empirical platform studies, similarity metrics, and toolkit development.

Recent directions emphasize temporal and semantic context, cognitively inspired algorithms, scalable social recommendation, and evaluation beyond accuracy—including the value of item embeddings for student job recommendations.

titles<=300|11c6da64f8be5834d42ca7a4ec70.text:
### Scalable Data Management for Scientific, Spatial, and Analytical Workloads

This community studies high-performance management and exploration of large, multidimensional, scientific, spatial, and graph-oriented datasets. Major themes include OLAP organization and estimation, relational backends for scientific applications, astronomical data services, spatial indexing and cross-matching, document and semantic search, and natural-language interfaces to databases.

Typical methods emphasize compact representations and fast execution: bitmap, inverted-index, integer, n-gram, and repetitive-text compression; roaring bitmaps; SIMD and vectorized decoding; GPU and CPU–GPU processing; in-memory SQL; caching, sorting, and attribute/row/column reordering; and specialized structures such as hierarchical triangular meshes, zone algorithms, Hippo indexes, and quasi-succinct indexes. Distributed, parallel, and cloud-based dataflows support batch processing, joins, graph mining, and low-latency scientific event analysis.

Recent work trends toward petabyte- and exascale-scale scientific metadata, full-lifecycle astronomical platforms, real-time analytics, trillion-cell interaction, and highly scalable in-memory systems. Natural-language querying is becoming more capable through SQL generation, query-log semantics, knowledge-rich interfaces, and neural models. Compression research increasingly combines theoretical guarantees with hardware-aware implementations, while analytics expands from traditional cubes toward relationships, entity graphs, cohorts, and complex geographic regions.

titles<=300|0714ee165dc101aa82625c89f93e.text:
### Scholarly Recommendation, Ranking, and Evaluation

This community focuses on building and evaluating recommender and ranking systems for scholarly information. Major themes include related-article and repository recommendation, research-paper and citation-parser recommendation, university ranking through Twitter engagement, sponsored-search ranking, and semantic publishing through information extraction and interlinking.

Typical methods combine learning-to-rank, deep reinforcement learning, meta-learning, rules and machine learning, expert-search-engine comparison, and user modeling based on mind maps or rich preference elicitation. Large-scale infrastructure is prominent: Apache Hadoop supports algorithm ecosystems and citation matching, while MR-DLIB provides recommendation services, APIs, and operational experience. Datasets include large related-article collections and dense user-feedback resources.

Evaluation is a central concern. The papers study biased feedback and position bias, advocate unbiased comparative evaluation and active sampling, compare offline with online testing, examine expert versus search-engine rankings, and assess choice overload. They also argue for temporal considerations and partially randomized results to improve evaluation validity.

Recent directions represented here emphasize deployable recommender services, larger datasets, scalable processing, individualized user information, bias correction, and more realistic online or time-aware evaluation.

titles<=300|fe4f2d0764eaf3e0f9855be0291f.text:
## Complex Event Processing and Scalable Stream Analytics

This community focuses on detecting, querying, and managing complex event patterns in high-volume, distributed streams. Core research includes foundations of complex event processing (CEP), SASE-based stream queries, join optimization, and efficient pattern detection using lazy chain automata. Load shedding addresses resource constraints, while work on consistent streaming emphasizes temporal coherence and reliable processing over time.

A second major theme is scalable data acquisition and inference for the Internet of Things. Distributed sensors and RFID systems motivate guaranteed time coherence, distributed query processing, and data-centric views of IoT data.

The papers commonly use automata-based event detection, stream query and join optimization, distributed inference, and systems-oriented performance evaluation. Benchmarking is especially prominent: several studies evaluate distributed stream-processing engines, while BigDataBench and BDGS provide benchmark suites and scalable synthetic data generation rooted in Internet services and web-search workloads. A related tool framework supports controlled feature variation in synthetic datasets.

Recent directions emphasize scaling CEP and stream processing across distributed infrastructures, improving temporal consistency and efficiency, and making evaluation more realistic and reproducible through domain-specific benchmarks and configurable data generators.

titles<=300|836525256634395aa6a832a4590d.text:
## Knowledge Organization Systems for the Semantic Web

This community examines how information objects, concepts, names, and relations can be represented and connected on the Web. A central theme is the transition from traditional library and cultural-heritage knowledge organization systems (KOS)—including LCSH and catalogs—to RDF, SKOS, and linked-data environments.

Research addresses the design choices, expressiveness, and machine processability of SKOS; the relationship between SKOS concepts and natural-language concepts; and the representation of literals, names, attributes, and catalog structures. Other studies investigate how metadata can function as reusable data, including models for publishing theses and dissertations as Web data.

Typical methods include ontological and conceptual analysis, multidimensional and literature reviews, close examination of standards and vocabularies, empirical quality assessment of SKOS datasets, latent-relationship analysis, and pragmatic case-based studies of libraries, archives, and museums.

Recent work trends toward operationalizing KOS for linked data: identifying quality problems, improving interoperability and machine processing, rethinking catalog visualization, and publishing institutional metadata as interconnected Web resources. The literature also highlights unresolved questions about what scholarly information should be preserved and how KOS structures can balance human interpretation with computational use.

titles<=300|6828ed99cf1ff1d47315fb8e8a65.text:
### Networked Analysis of Social, Health, and Information Systems

This community studies how network structure and large-scale digital traces can reveal behaviors, relationships, and biases. A major theme is public-health surveillance through social media: papers analyze illicit drug dealing, use, interactions, and adverse reactions on Instagram, while others examine e-cigarette flavors, brands, and markets through Reddit and Twitter. Image and multimodal analysis support fine-grained characterization of these phenomena.

A second theme is network-based recommendation and information organization, including Pinterest-to-Twitter board recommendation, semi-metric networks, document networks, and adaptive knowledge management. Related work applies network structure to collective document classification and to extracting protein interactions from scientific abstracts using word-proximity networks.

The community also addresses health-system inequities, with city-wide electronic health-record analysis identifying gender and age biases in the administration of known drug–drug interactions. Other work analyzes attitudes toward China in American tweets at state and individual levels and investigates distance closures in complex networks.

Typical methods combine social-media mining, textual and image analysis, multimodal signals, word-proximity and semi-metric networks, network analysis, linear models, and biologically inspired distributed designs. Recent trends emphasize fine-grained, cross-platform, comparative, and population-scale monitoring of health and social behavior.

titles<=300|07d58015d836a70e7741c1de0d30.text:
## Scholarly Recommendation, Extraction, and Literature Intelligence

This community focuses on improving how scientific literature is parsed, linked, evaluated, and recommended. Major themes include research-paper and related-article recommendation; citation recommendation and matching; biomedical hypothesis generation; scholarly knowledge graphs and semantic publishing; metadata, author-contribution, and OCR-based information extraction; and analysis of text reuse, plagiarism, authorship, and citation behavior.

Typical methods combine collaborative filtering, content features, keyphrases, terms, document embeddings, citation context, reference-string and segment features, topic-driven ranking, mind-map user models, and hybrid architectures. Machine learning is frequently compared with rules and off-the-shelf versus retrained parsers. Meta-learning is used to select recommendation algorithms per instance, while Hadoop supports large-scale processing. Evaluation increasingly relies on massive datasets, online living labs, expert and search-engine rankings, click behavior, choice-overload analysis, position-bias studies, and time-aware metrics.

Recent trends include pretrained language models and navigation-based candidate expansion for citation recommendation, scalable commercial-style recommender services, large related-article datasets, explainable tuning of opaque models, and automated biomedical hypothesis generation. The literature also emphasizes operational challenges—building and maintaining real-world systems—and richer scholarly infrastructure, including CL Scholar, GrapAL, and semantic interlinking.

titles<=300|9c02229202fcd1fcf72c1b5b9861.text:
### Decentralized Online Social Networks: Architectures and Governance

This community focuses on designing and understanding peer-to-peer (P2P) online social networks as alternatives to centralized platforms. Its main themes include decentralized system architectures, social-network functionality, scalability, resource organization, and policy enforcement across independently managed nodes.

Typical methods are architectural proposals, framework design, and comprehensive surveys. The papers examine different organizational models, including fully P2P systems and super-peer architectures, where selected peers coordinate or provide enhanced services. They also address how global policies can be established and maintained in decentralized environments, highlighting governance as a central systems challenge.

The research trajectory progresses from foundational analysis of P2P-based social networks toward concrete next-generation designs and implementations. “MyZone,” “SuperNova,” and “LibreSocial” represent efforts to define practical platforms or reusable frameworks, while the work on global policies addresses cross-system coordination and control. Overall, the community reflects a trend toward more structured, policy-aware, and deployable decentralized social-network architectures rather than purely conceptual P2P models.

titles<=300|68c8ab18ce6bad215604bf4c4cba.text:
## Query Languages, Expressiveness, and Scalable Data Processing

This community studies how query languages and database systems represent, optimize, and evaluate information across structured, heterogeneous, and distributed data. Major themes include querying trees and complex-value databases, web information extraction, and the expressive power of formal languages such as monadic Datalog and guarded-negation queries. Several papers focus on structural restrictions—particularly finite structures and bounded treewidth—to characterize tractability and expressiveness.

A second theme is scalable query processing. Work on randomized computation, streaming, and external-memory data establishes tight lower bounds, clarifying the limits of efficient processing on large datasets. Systems-oriented contributions include Apache Calcite’s framework for optimized queries over heterogeneous sources, database operations in D4M.jl, and curator-based provenance management for distributed systems.

Typical methods combine formal language and logic analysis, complexity-theoretic lower bounds, query-language design, and system/framework construction. Visual interfaces appear in work on web-wrapper generators and visual queries for complex values. Recent trends point toward integration: expressive query languages are being studied alongside practical optimization, heterogeneous and distributed execution, provenance, and scalable data management.

titles<=300|b15845aea629f260439c80c62543.text:
## Novelty, Discovery, and Text-Based Retrieval

This community studies how scientific and technological knowledge is discovered, evaluated, and advanced. A central theme is the relationship between **novelty or surprise** and future impact, including the effect of grant novelty on later scientific influence and the role of surprising combinations in science and technology progress.

A second theme is **interactive exploration**, represented by PubVis, which supports discovery and navigation of scientific publications. The community also develops **text-based similarity and retrieval methods**, including textual spatial cosine similarity and full-text similarity search for automating patent prior-art searches. A literature review further consolidates approaches to patent retrieval.

Typical methods combine empirical analysis of scientific impact, interactive visualization, computational text similarity, and information-retrieval techniques applied to patents and publications. An emerging trend is the integration of scalable textual analysis with user-facing exploration tools, enabling more systematic discovery while also investigating how unexpected or novel work shapes subsequent advancement.

titles<=300|dba3feb62b7fdb51cd8452ea50f9.text:
### Formal Querying and Validation of Workflow Graphs

This community studies structured graph data, especially workflow representations and provenance. Its main themes are expressive pattern matching, dependency-aware labeling, semantic annotation quality, and schema customization.

Typical methods include tree-pattern queries extended with logical operators; regular path queries for navigating workflow provenance; and stack-based algorithms for matching patterns on directed acyclic graphs. The work also emphasizes formal verification and validation of semantic annotations, alongside SHACL-based approaches for customizing schema organizations. Fine-grained dependency information is used to label workflow views, suggesting a focus on preserving and exposing structure during analysis.

Across the papers, the research trends toward combining richer query languages with scalable graph algorithms and stronger semantic guarantees. Querying is becoming more expressive—from tree patterns to logical and regular-path formulations—while validation and SHACL provide mechanisms for ensuring that graph annotations and schemas remain consistent. DAG-specific algorithmic analysis complements these declarative and formal approaches, particularly for workflow and provenance settings.

titles<=300|abdb7b09895895ca776718d4de82.text:
## Graph Analytics, Utility Mining, and Temporal Networks

This community combines scalable graph algorithms with pattern and utility-oriented data mining. A major theme is efficient querying on large, dynamic, directed, and temporal graphs: reachability oracles, shortest-path and distance labeling, landmark sketches, hub acceleration, hop doubling, and distributed or vertex-centric computation. Window analytics, time-based paths, and temporal-network indicators extend these methods to evolving social and knowledge graphs.

A second focus is sequential and episode mining. Work addresses frequent, closed, non-derivable, compressing, and constrained episodes, including simultaneous events and complex or uncertain sequences. Utility mining generalizes frequency-based discovery through item-specific or individualized thresholds, multidimensional and multiple sequences, trend information, and privacy preservation. Pattern summarization, association-rule bases, and statistical significance improve interpretability and reliability.

Applications include revenue-maximizing recommendations, trust-aware social recommendation, social-content matching, spatiotextual clustering, route and POI search, opinion diffusion, and scientific-network evolution. Typical methods include pruning, projection, submodularity, MapReduce, distributed processing, indexing, and provable performance or approximation guarantees.

Recent directions emphasize dynamic and temporal graphs, scalable distributed execution, personalized utility criteria, uncertain data, privacy, and integrating analytical queries with large-scale graph systems.

titles<=300|95068d25b31fae176e6f2e3d7c67.text:
## Search, Ranking, and Efficient Data Systems

This community spans information retrieval, database query processing, recommender systems, and data-intensive analytics. Core themes include top-*k*, skyline, preference, similarity, and aggregate queries over relational, graph, spatial, streaming, and hidden-web data. Search research addresses crawling, query variation, reranking, retrieval over sequences and semantic data, sponsored search, and scientific literature discovery.

A major strand concerns fairness, diversity, and exposure in rankings and recommendations, including position bias, disparate exposure, polarization, representation bias, and unbiased learning-to-rank. Applications include talent search, digital libraries, academia, social media, and participatory content. Scientific recommender systems, citation matching, expert recommendation, and bibliographic parsing are recurring domains.

Typical methods include exact and approximate algorithms, skyline and dominance techniques, preference elicitation, learning-to-rank, reinforcement learning, meta-learning, graph and game-theoretic models, clustering, and entity resolution. Systems work emphasizes SIMD/GPU acceleration, compressed and roaring bitmap indexes, integer and inverted-index compression, learned indexes, distributed dataflow, caching, and in-memory analytics.

Recent directions emphasize fairness-aware and partially randomized ranking, neural or deep-RL optimization, evaluation without relevance judgments, large-scale scientific and social datasets, real-time streaming, and scalable graph or hidden-database querying.

titles<=300|a1fd6cb9c45df1f7af450fed9b36.text:
## Graph Representation Learning in Dynamic and Heterogeneous Networks

This community focuses on modeling, analyzing, and learning from complex networks, especially social, temporal, heterogeneous, signed, multilayer, and knowledge graphs. Major tasks include link prediction, community detection, node classification and role identification, anomaly and fraud detection, recommendation, network alignment, and graph similarity search.

Typical methods combine random walks, matrix factorization, graph sampling, motif and graphlet statistics, spectral and centrality-based analysis, stochastic blockmodels, latent-space and graph-generative models, and graph neural networks. Representation learning is prominent, including DeepWalk, node2vec, struc2vec, metapath-guided embeddings, graph convolutional and attention networks, autoencoders, adversarial models, and multimodal approaches integrating text, attributes, and network structure.

A strong methodological emphasis is scalability: distributed and GPU algorithms address triangle, motif, betweenness, and subgraph counting, while sampling, sparsification, coarsening, and external-memory techniques support massive graphs. Temporal research increasingly models event streams, evolving communities, dynamic embeddings, link persistence, change points, and time-aware prediction. Recent work also emphasizes robustness and reliability through adversarial attacks, privacy, sampling bias, missing links, uncertain networks, and improved evaluation frameworks. Applications span social media, recommender systems, finance and fraud, scholarly and patent networks, web navigation, online communities, and knowledge-graph reasoning.

titles<=300|28fe121569916866e634d4b44395.text:
## Cognitive, Temporal, and Graph-Based Recommendation

This community focuses on recommendation under sparsity, cold start, evolving user interests, and the distinctive structure of social tagging and folksonomies. A major theme is cognitive-inspired tag recommendation: models explain tag reuse through frequency, recency, semantic context, forgetting, activation, and memory processes. Related work studies hashtag reuse and confirmation bias in Twitter.

Typical methods combine temporal and semantic features, collaborative filtering, trust and regular equivalence, link-analysis algorithms for bipartite graphs, and resource-ranking techniques. Recommendation settings include social tags, spatial items, student jobs, and users at home or away, with geographical and sentiment-aware models addressing context. Similarity-search papers develop top-*k* joins and self-joins for streaming or endless data.

Recent directions emphasize hybrid and representation-based approaches, including attention-inspired resource recommendation, deep learning for large-scale cold start, and item embeddings evaluated beyond accuracy. Other work proposes nonstandard similarity and graph-sur surfing methods, while cognitive algorithms seek better alignment between recommender outputs and real-world folksonomy structure. Overall, the community combines behavioral modeling, temporal dynamics, graph methods, and scalable stream processing to improve personalized recommendation.

titles<=300|6a7b0b2684b4c64590907ce2564d.text:
## Scholarly Recommendation, Metadata, and Literature Mining

This community focuses on improving access to and discovery of scientific literature through recommendation, metadata extraction, and scholarly knowledge graphs. A major theme is recommender-system design, including scalable hybrid systems, collaborative-filtering algorithm recommendation (CF4CF), and meta-learning approaches that select recommendation algorithms per instance or at a micro level. Evaluation is emphasized through online living-lab experiments, related-article datasets, and analyses of click, purchase, and other impact-oriented metrics.

A second theme is richer scholarly representation and discovery. GrapAL, NLPExplorer, and CL Scholar connect papers, concepts, authors, and references through graph-based or knowledge-graph mining approaches, supporting exploration of research fields. Other work extracts author contributions and general metadata from scientific publications, while ExMatcher improves citation matching by combining reference-string and document-segment features.

Typical methods combine collaborative filtering, hybrid feature models, meta-learning, document embeddings, keyphrases, terms, natural-language processing, graph construction, and information extraction. Recent trends include per-instance adaptive recommendation, scalable online evaluation, richer datasets, and comparisons of representation choices—especially embeddings versus traditional textual features—alongside more structured and interconnected scholarly discovery.

titles<=300|39949184c2e9787c71b36ca7ea83.text:
### Scalable and Accessible Data Management
